Estuary Freight Outlook Turns Negative as Bond Refinancing Remains Unresolved

By Tomas Arven and Céline Maret
September 4, 2026

Northstar Credit Analytics has affirmed Estuary Freight's BBB- senior unsecured bond rating and revised the outlook to negative from stable. The Kestrel Bay cargo handler has KRN 160 million of bonds falling due in February 2027. Discussions with lenders are continuing, but the company has not secured replacement funding.

At 31 July, Estuary Freight held KRN 38 million in unrestricted cash and had KRN 25 million available under committed facilities. Cargo volumes fell 6% in the first seven months of the year, mainly because of lower building material shipments. Northstar estimates debt at 4.4 times annual operating profit before depreciation, against 3.8 times at the end of 2025.

The negative outlook reflects the narrowing time available to refinance. Northstar could lower the rating if funding arrangements remain incomplete or operating performance weakens further. A return to a stable outlook would require sufficient committed funding to repay the bonds and evidence that cargo earnings have steadied.

Half-year sales rise as GreenBasket reports lower operating profit

30 September 2026Daniel Rooke, Corporate Affairs

GreenBasket Supermarkets, Kestria's largest supermarket chain by store count, reported revenue of KRN 6.42 billion for the 26 weeks ended 30 August 2026, up 4.1 per cent on the comparable period. Sales at stores open for at least a year rose 2.7 per cent.

Operating profit fell from KRN 206 million to KRN 193 million. Higher wage and refrigeration maintenance costs outweighed savings in distribution. GreenBasket invested KRN 118 million in stores, equipment and delivery vehicles during the period, including the Eastmere opening in Amberford. It ended the half year with 215 stores.

Finance director Anika Pell said customers were buying more own-label groceries and making smaller, more frequent trips. Own-label products accounted for 58 per cent of grocery units sold, compared with 55 per cent a year earlier. Online orders represented 9.4 per cent of revenue, up from 8.7 per cent in the comparable period.

Small suppliers receive shorter payment terms under new purchasing policy

26 August 2026Idris Weller, Corporate Affairs

GreenBasket Supermarkets has introduced payment terms of 14 calendar days for qualifying small suppliers, replacing its previous standard of 30 days. The policy applies to new purchase orders issued from today. A total of 186 existing suppliers meet the published eligibility rules.

Procurement director Nella Corven said smaller producers often paid wages and bought materials well before receiving money for their goods. Bracken Grid Bond Rating Holds After Amberford Storm Disruption

By Tomas Arven and Mara Vellin
October 9, 2026

Northstar Credit Analytics has maintained Bracken Grid's BBB senior unsecured bond rating and stable outlook following the 6 October storm in the Amberford district. The storm damaged overhead lines and interrupted supplies to 74,000 connections. By the evening of 8 October, the company had restored power to all but 1,900 affected connections.

Bracken Grid's preliminary estimate places repair costs at KRN 18 million to KRN 24 million. Northstar has assumed the full upper estimate in its initial assessment without relying on insurance receipts. The company had KRN 72 million in cash and KRN 110 million of undrawn committed facilities at the end of September.

These resources should allow repairs to proceed without materially weakening liquidity. The rating also allows for occasional weather-related disruption. Northstar will review the final repair bill, compensation payments and any changes to planned maintenance. Costs substantially above the current estimate, or evidence of wider network weaknesses, could alter the assessment.

Ostara Rental Housing Outlook Remains Stable Despite Higher Maintenance Spending

By Mara Vellin and Dario Selven
October 8, 2026

Northstar Credit Analytics has maintained a stable sector outlook for rated rental housing companies operating in Ostara. High occupancy and steady rent collection continue to support earnings, although repairs and borrowing costs are absorbing more cash. The assessment covers four issuers with a combined 28,400 homes.

Average occupancy stood at 97.4% at the end of August, compared with 97.1% a year earlier. Rent arrears remained modest at 1.8% of annual billed rent. Maintenance spending rose 8%, led by roof repairs and heating replacements. Fixed interest rates apply to 76% of the sample's debt, limiting the immediate effect of higher financing costs.

Northstar expects most issuers to fund routine repairs from rental income while keeping development programmes within committed borrowing limits. Ratings could come under pressure where large construction projects coincide with debt maturities. The stable sector outlook assumes occupancy remains above 96% and companies retain enough accessible funding to meet twelve months of planned spending.

Ostara depot changes cut damaged produce deliveries by nearly a quarter

8 October 2026Idris Weller, Corporate Affairs

GreenBasket Supermarkets has reduced damaged fruit and vegetable deliveries from its Ostara depot by 24 per cent following changes to packing and loading. The result compares damage recorded per thousand crates during July to September with the same three months of 2025.

The depot supplies 68 stores and handles about 410,000 produce crates each month. Changes included shallower crates for soft fruit, separate loading positions for heavier root vegetables and temperature checks at each loading bay. GreenBasket spent KRN 1.7 million on equipment and training for the work.

Depot manager Brenna Holt said staff had recorded where damage occurred before changing handling routines. The measured reduction represents approximately 7,800 fewer damaged crates over the quarter. Produce rejected by stores remains subject to the same quality checks, and items suitable for sale are assessed separately from stock that must be discarded.

GreenBasket Supermarkets is recalling its 250-gram Honeyfield Oat Biscuits with batch code HB0902 and a best-before date of 18 February 2027. The affected packs contain milk, which is missing from the allergen statement. They are unsuitable for people with a milk allergy.

The biscuits were sold in 87 GreenBasket stores across Kestria between 3 and 8 September. Customers with a milk allergy should not eat them. Anyone who bought an affected pack can return it to any GreenBasket store for a full refund without a receipt. Other batch codes are not included in this recall.

GreenBasket identified the error during a packaging check yesterday and removed the affected stock from sale that evening. Recall notices are displayed in the relevant stores and on the customer website. Product safety manager Orla Venn said the company had received no reports of illness linked to the affected batch.

Estuary Freight Downgraded to BB as Refinancing Options Narrow

By Tomas Arven and Dario Selven
October 15, 2026

Northstar Credit Analytics has lowered Estuary Freight's senior unsecured bond rating to BB from BBB- and concluded the review opened on 13 October. The outlook is negative. Further information supplied during the review shows that the company has limited readily available funding for its KRN 160 million February 2027 bond repayment.

Of the KRN 25 million previously reported as available under committed facilities, KRN 15 million expires in January 2027. Northstar therefore excludes that amount when assessing resources for the bond maturity. The proposed storage yard sale remains at an early stage, with no agreed buyer or binding timetable. September cargo earnings also fell below management's revised budget.

The downgrade principally reflects weaker refinancing prospects and reduced financial flexibility. The revised liquidity methodology published yesterday also informs the assessment of facility availability. The negative outlook indicates further downside if replacement funding remains unsecured. A stable outlook would require a credible, committed repayment plan and enough cash to continue ordinary operations.

Val-Brume Packaging Downgraded to BB+ Following Weaker Cash Generation

By Elise Dorne and Dario Selven
September 24, 2026

Northstar Credit Analytics has lowered Val-Brume Packaging's senior unsecured bond rating to BB+ from BBB-. The outlook is stable. The producer of cartons and food containers has reported weaker earnings and a larger working capital requirement than Northstar assumed in its previous review.

Operating profit before depreciation fell 22% to KRN 41 million in the year ended July, while debt increased to KRN 205 million. Higher paper input costs and slower customer payments contributed to the deterioration. Debt reached 5.0 times operating profit, compared with 3.6 times a year earlier. The company serves food producers across Kestria from its principal factory in Val-Brume.

Cash of KRN 19 million and an undrawn committed facility of KRN 35 million provide adequate near-term funding. No bond principal is due before 2029. The stable outlook assumes tighter stock control and lower investment spending prevent further debt growth. Another downgrade could follow if cash generation remains negative or available funding falls materially.

Words by Tobin Rusk

28 Sep 2026

Lumen Home Retail will shorten opening hours at its Kestrel Bay Harbour Lane branch while contractors replace part of the roof. From 5 to 16 October, the store will open from 9 am to 6 pm each day. Its usual opening hours are 7 am to 9 pm.

GreenBasket publishes clearer rules for supplier deductions and invoice disputes

15 October 2026Idris Weller, Corporate Affairs

GreenBasket Supermarkets has introduced a supplier code covering invoice disputes, delivery deductions and changes to orders. Effective today, the code requires buyers to provide written reasons and supporting records before making a deduction. It applies to all goods suppliers across the company's 216 stores.

Val-Brume Packaging Rating Affirmed After Investment Spending Is Reduced

By Céline Maret and Dario Selven
October 22, 2026

Northstar Credit Analytics has affirmed Val-Brume Packaging's BB+ senior unsecured bond rating and stable outlook after the company reduced its investment budget. Management has deferred a second printing line, cutting planned spending for the current financial year to KRN 18 million from KRN 34 million.

The decision preserves cash while the company addresses the working capital pressures behind its September downgrade. Unrestricted cash stood at KRN 22 million at the end of September, with KRN 35 million still available under its committed facility. Early collections from overdue customers helped the improvement, although one month of stronger receipts does not establish a sustained recovery.

Northstar continues to expect debt near 5.0 times annual operating profit before depreciation in the near term. The revised liquidity assessment supports the existing rating because available resources cover projected seasonal needs. An upgrade would require durable earnings recovery and lower debt. Renewed cash outflows, weaker facility access or substantial additional borrowing could lead to another downgrade.

Kestrian Retail Bond Issuers Enter Winter with Uneven Cash Buffers

By Elise Dorne and Nalin Verdan
October 20, 2026

Northstar Credit Analytics has maintained a negative outlook for Kestrian discretionary retailers in its latest sector review. Households are limiting larger purchases, while retailers have already paid for much of their winter stock. The agency expects differences in cash reserves to matter more than modest changes in reported sales.

Among six rated issuers, stock values at the end of September were 9% higher than a year earlier, while sales for the preceding three months rose only 1%. Two chains operating mainly in Saltmarsh and Kestrel Bay increased promotional discounts to clear older goods. Across the sample, average operating margins before depreciation fell to 6.2% from 7.1%.

Four issuers have committed facilities extending beyond their seasonal borrowing peak. The remaining two rely more heavily on cash generated during winter trading. Northstar is testing slower stock sales and delayed supplier credit separately for each company. The sector outlook does not imply that every retailer will be downgraded, and no individual rating changes accompany this report.

September employment increases while unemployment rate remains unchanged

Tovan Merrow · Head of Labour Market Statistics · 16 October 2026

Employment in Kestria increased by an estimated 6,000 in September to 2,849,000. The seasonally adjusted unemployment rate remained at 5.5 per cent, with 166,000 people unemployed. The employment rate for people aged 16 to 64 returned to 73.1 per cent, the same rate recorded in July.

Health and social care, education and business support recorded employment gains. Manufacturing employment was broadly stable. More people entered the labour force during the month, allowing employment to rise without a fall in the unemployment rate. The labour force includes everyone who is employed or meets the survey definition of unemployment.

In the three months to September, employment averaged 2,846,000. This was 9,000 higher than in the three months to June. Regional estimates, including those for Saltmarsh and Val-Brume, are published as three-month averages because their smaller survey samples make single-month comparisons less dependable. All figures remain subject to sampling uncertainty.

August labour survey shows a small rise in unemployment

Tovan Merrow · Head of Labour Market Statistics · 16 September 2026

The seasonally adjusted unemployment rate rose to 5.5 per cent in August, from 5.4 per cent in July. Employment was estimated at 2,843,000, down by 3,000 over the month. The number of unemployed people increased by 4,000 to 166,000, while the number outside the labour force changed little.

Accommodation and food services recorded fewer workers after July's increase. Employment in health and social care continued to grow. The employment rate for people aged 16 to 64 was 73.0 per cent. Average weekly hours worked were broadly stable, with no clear change in the balance between full-time and part-time work.

The monthly movements are small relative to the uncertainty around the survey estimates. Results for the three months to August show employment above its level in the previous three months. The Kestria Statistics Office recommends using that wider comparison when assessing the direction of the labour market.

Kestrel Bay branch sets temporary hours during roof repairs

28 Sep 2026

Lumen Home Retail will shorten opening hours at its Kestrel Bay Harbour Lane branch while contractors replace part of the roof. From 5 to 16 October, the store will open from 9 am to 6 pm each day. Its usual opening hours are 7 am to 9 pm.

A routine building inspection found worn seals above the homeware stockroom. The affected storage area has been cleared, and work will take place behind a separate barrier. The repair budget is KRN 640,000. Grocery shopping, the pharmacy counter and customer toilets will remain available during the temporary opening hours.

Online collection customers with bookings outside the revised hours will be contacted directly and offered another slot or free home delivery. Staff will retain their contracted pay, with some shifts moved to stock preparation and nearby delivery operations. Lumen expects normal hours to resume on 17 October, subject to the final building inspection.

Lumen Home Retail has completed a KRN 1.8 million refurbishment of its Amberford Millgate store. The work adds a separate collection counter beside the main entrance, wider aisles in the grocery section and clearer signs for household essentials. Corvel updates carton prices following higher board costs

By Ellis Dacre · September 30, 2026
Share: LinkedIn X Email

Corvel Packaging has increased base prices for newly quoted folding cartons by an average of 3.4 per cent from today. Individual changes range from 2.1 to 4.6 per cent, depending on board grade, carton weight and print requirements. Confirmed orders retain their agreed base prices.

The adjustment follows higher delivered board costs recorded during August and September. It applies to cartons produced at Amberford and does not change the base prices of trays or films. The energy surcharge remains separate at KRN 58 per tonne and is calculated using dispatch weight.

Revised quotations show the base price and estimated surcharge separately so customers can compare the full cost at a stated order quantity. Existing written quotations remain valid until their stated expiry dates. Account teams can review board grades or order sizes with customers, although any specification change still requires approval before production.

Ostara tray plant cuts trim waste through tooling changes

By Tobin Merrow · September 29, 2026
Share: LinkedIn X Email

Corvel Packaging's Ostara plant has reduced trim waste on two chilled-food tray lines following changes to cutting tools and sheet positioning. Across eight weeks of measured production, trim represented 13.1 per cent of material fed into the lines, down from 16.4 per cent during the preceding eight weeks.

The comparison covers the same four tray designs and excludes trial runs. Staff adjusted the spacing between tray shapes and replaced worn cutting edges. The plant used 18 tonnes less sheet material than it would have used at the earlier trim rate for the recorded volume.

Tray dimensions, sealing surfaces and approved material specifications are unchanged. Clean trim from these lines is separated for controlled reprocessing, subject to the requirements of each product specification. Corvel is reporting the reduction as a material efficiency measure; it has not calculated a carbon saving from the work.

Harvest Review Trims Wheat Estimate As Oat Outlook Holds

AMBERFORD, Kestria, Sept. 28, 2026 /KestriaWire/ -- Prairie Gold Grain Co-operative has revised its member wheat harvest estimate to 179,500 tonnes, down from the August estimate of 184,000 tonnes. The oat estimate is now 52,400 tonnes, compared with 52,000 tonnes previously. The review uses completed field records and updated reports received by 27 September.

Lower wheat yields around Ostara account for most of the reduction. Amberford results remain close to the earlier estimate. Members report that 81 per cent of their wheat area and 69 per cent of their oat area has been harvested, leaving uncertainty around the remaining fields.

The co-operative has accepted 96,800 tonnes of wheat and 21,600 tonnes of oats into its stores. These intake figures exclude grain still held on farms and must not be added to the harvest estimate. Customer allocations remain covered by accepted stocks and grain secured under existing member delivery agreements.

Prairie Gold is owned by 4,100 farming families and handles about a fifth of Kestria's wheat and oat harvest.

Rain Raises Drying Demand At Ostara Grain Receiving Site

AMBERFORD, Kestria, Sept. 16, 2026 /KestriaWire/ -- Rain around Ostara has increased the proportion of wheat deliveries requiring drying at Prairie Gold Grain Co-operative's local receiving site. Of the 61 wheat loads sampled during the past two days, 24 exceeded the standard moisture limit of 14 per cent. Accepted wet grain is being stored separately.

The site's dryer has processed 460 tonnes since the rain began. Members are being given a moisture reading and an estimated drying charge before unloading. The charge depends on the moisture removed and is separate from the purchase price shown on the member's grain agreement.

Receiving staff have reduced the number of wet-grain bookings to match drying capacity. Dry wheat and oat bookings remain available, subject to storage space. Members should report their latest moisture reading when arranging a delivery and should not mix damp grain with a dry load to meet the acceptance limit.

Val-Brume stores introduce clearer French labels across household essentials

6 Oct 2026

Lumen Home Retail has introduced clearer French-language shelf labels at its three Val-Brume stores. The change covers 2,300 household and grocery products, including cleaning supplies, bedding and cupboard staples. Product names, pack sizes and unit prices now appear together in a larger, consistent format.

The work follows an eight-week review with customers and store colleagues in Kestria's French-speaking region. Participants said that unit prices were sometimes difficult to locate and that several household product descriptions needed simpler wording. Printed guidance at service desks and online collection instructions have also been revised.

The project cost KRN 210,000, including translation, printing and staff training. It does not change product prices or the ranges stocked. Lumen will collect feedback at the three stores through November and check a sample of labels each week for accuracy. Customers can report unclear wording at any service desk or through the retailer's website.

New Ostara bakery agreement brings daily deliveries to more stores

16 Sep 2026

Lumen Home Retail has signed a three-year supply agreement with Hearthmere Baking, a family-owned producer based in Ostara. From 21 September, the bakery will supply bread and rolls to 14 Lumen stores, extending an existing arrangement covering six branches. The agreement is worth an estimated KRN 7.2 million over its term.

Hearthmere has installed an additional oven and created nine production and packing jobs to support the wider service. Deliveries will reach stores before opening on six mornings each week. The range includes a small sliced loaf developed after customers asked for more choices suited to smaller households.

Lumen will provide weekly order forecasts and pay agreed invoices within 21 days. Both businesses will review unsold quantities each month, with the aim of reducing surplus without leaving shelves empty late in the day. Existing bakery suppliers will continue serving Lumen stores outside the expanded delivery area.

Quarterly trade tables show growth in services exports

Nessa Talvern · Head of Trade Statistics · 22 October 2026

Kestria exported services worth KRN 3.24 billion in the second quarter of 2026, an increase of 4.2 per cent from the first quarter. Services imports rose by 2.0 per cent to KRN 2.61 billion. The resulting services surplus was KRN 630 million, according to quarterly tables published today.

Business support and remote technical services accounted for most of the export increase. Transport services also grew, with higher receipts reported by operators based in Kestrel Bay. Travel spending by visitors increased modestly. The figures are seasonally adjusted and measured at current prices, so growth can reflect both higher prices and increased activity.

Services trade is measured mainly through business surveys and administrative records, rather than the border declarations used for goods. It is published later because the necessary information takes longer to collect. These second-quarter figures should not be combined directly with July or August goods figures to calculate a monthly overall trade balance.

August goods imports rise faster than export values

Nessa Talvern · Head of Trade Statistics · 9 October 2026

Kestria's goods trade deficit widened to KRN 710 million in August, from KRN 540 million in July. Exports totalled KRN 4.86 billion and imports totalled KRN 5.57 billion. Seasonally adjusted export values increased by 0.8 per cent over the month, while import values increased by 3.9 per cent.

Higher machinery and fuel imports contributed most to the wider deficit. Export growth was concentrated in processed food, while electrical equipment exports declined slightly after July's increase. Businesses in the Ostara industrial area reported several large machinery deliveries, illustrating how individual purchases can affect monthly trade totals.

Over the three months to August, exports were 1.7 per cent higher than in the previous three months and imports were 2.2 per cent higher. These comparisons use values at current prices. They therefore reflect changes in prices as well as quantities. July totals are unchanged from the previous release.

Kestrel Bay Loading Repairs Restore Normal Grain Dispatch Capacity

OSTARA, Kestria, Oct. 6, 2026 /KestriaWire/ -- Prairie Gold Grain Co-operative has restored normal dispatch capacity at its Kestrel Bay store after replacing a worn bearing in the grain loading conveyor. The conveyor returned to service on 5 October following an inspection and an unloaded test. Grain receiving continued while the equipment was unavailable.

The interruption delayed nine customer collections carrying a combined 270 tonnes of wheat and oats. Six have now been completed, and revised collection times have been agreed for the remaining three. No grain was damaged, and the affected conveyor did not require any stored stock to be discarded.

The loading line is again operating at its normal rate of up to 90 tonnes an hour, subject to vehicle changes and sampling. Customers should use the collection time shown on their latest dispatch confirmation. Drivers arriving early must wait in the marked parking area until called to the loading point.

About Prairie Gold Grain Co-operative
Prairie Gold is owned by 4,100 farming families and handles about a fifth of Kestria's wheat and oat harvest.

Early Wheat Samples Show Firm Protein And Low Moisture

OSTARA, Kestria, Sept. 7, 2026 /KestriaWire/ -- The first new-season quality report from Prairie Gold Grain Co-operative shows average wheat protein of 12.6 per cent and average moisture of 13.2 per cent. The report covers 186 accepted loads, representing 5,920 tonnes delivered to the Amberford and Ostara receiving sites by 6 September.

Average wheat test weight was 78.4 kilogrammes per hectolitre. These results support the sale of several parcels for milling, although each customer contract has its own requirements. The samples mainly represent earlier-harvested fields and should not be treated as a measure of the whole crop.

Oat deliveries remain limited, with 740 tonnes accepted so far. Members can request the test results for their own loads through the receiving office. Any request for a second test must identify the delivery ticket, allowing staff to locate the sealed sample retained from that load.

Corvel publishes evidence sheets for selected carton recycling claims

By Tobin Merrow · October 9, 2026
Share: LinkedIn X Email

Corvel Packaging has issued evidence sheets for 18 uncoated carton specifications supplied from Amberford. Each sheet identifies the board grade, coatings, inks and adhesives covered by the assessment. It also explains the conditions attached to the company's recycling statements.

The sheets draw on fibre separation tests and checks of collection guidance available in Saltmarsh, Amberford and Val-Brume. Results apply only to the listed specifications. Cartons with film windows, barrier layers or heavy food contamination require separate consideration and are outside the scope of this release.

Customers can request a sheet using their carton specification number. The documents support packaging decisions but do not establish that every local collection service accepts a carton. Corvel advises customers to check disposal wording against the collection arrangements serving their buyers. No new recycling claim has been added to customer artwork as part of this work.

Ostara tray plant cuts trim waste through tooling changes

By Tobin Merrow · September 29, 2026
Share: LinkedIn X Email

Corvel Packaging's Ostara plant has reduced trim waste on two chilled-food tray lines following changes to cutting tools and sheet positioning. Across eight weeks of measured production, trim represented 13.1 per cent of material fed into the lines, down from 16.4 per cent during the preceding eight weeks.

The comparison covers the same four tray designs and excludes trial runs. Staff adjusted the spacing between tray shapes and replaced worn cutting edges. The plant used 18 tonnes less sheet material than it would have used at the earlier trim rate for the recorded volume.

Tray dimensions, sealing surfaces and approved material specifications are unchanged. Clean trim from these lines is separated for controlled reprocessing, subject to the requirements of each product specification. Corvel is reporting the reduction as a material efficiency measure; it has not calculated a carbon saving from the work.

Bramble Foods pays interim dividend of twelve crowns cents

By Mara Fenwick

30 September 2026

Bramble Foods today paid its interim dividend of KRN 0.12 per ordinary share to shareholders who were on the register on 4 September 2026. The payment follows the dividend declaration included in the company's half-year results on 17 August. The total distribution is KRN 7.2 million.

Shareholders receiving payment by bank transfer should allow for their bank's normal processing times. Those who have elected to receive paper payment notices will receive them at their registered address. Dividend statements are also available through the company's shareholder account service.

Bramble Foods reports higher first half sales and operating profit

By Mara Fenwick

17 August 2026

Bramble Foods, the listed Kestrian bakery and snacks company, today reported revenue of KRN 428.6 million for the six months ended 30 June 2026, up 6.4% on the same period last year. Operating profit rose to KRN 34.2 million from KRN 30.8 million. Sales volumes increased by 2.1%, with the remaining revenue growth coming from prices and changes in the mix of products sold.

Packaged bread performed steadily, while savoury crackers and small cake packs recorded stronger growth. Lower waste at the Amberford bakery helped offset higher flour and packaging costs. Net debt at the period end was KRN 76.5 million, compared with KRN 81.3 million a year earlier.

The board declared an interim dividend of KRN 0.12 per share, payable on 30 September to shareholders registered on 4 September. Bramble Foods continues to expect modest volume growth during the second half, although household spending remains uneven across Kestria.

Corvel adds recycled content option for selected food trays

By Tobin Merrow · October 15, 2026
Share: LinkedIn X Email

Corvel Packaging has added a tray material containing 35 per cent recycled plastic by weight to its Ostara product range. The option is available for two clear chilled-food tray sizes. It uses recycled material from a controlled process assessed for the specified food contact conditions.

Qualification checks covered material traceability, tray strength, sealing and migration under chilled storage conditions. The trays are approved for the listed chilled foods and temperatures in their technical sheets. They are not approved for oven use. Customers must confirm that their intended food and filling process match those conditions.

Sign up for our monthly update on packaging prices, new products and sustainability. You can unsubscribe at any time.

The recycled content figure applies to the tray body and excludes any lid, label or absorbent pad. Batch records identify the material blend used in production. Initial supply is available in minimum orders of 40,000 trays per size, with pricing provided by quotation. Existing tray specifications remain available for customers with different requirements.

AMBERFORD, Kestria, Sept. 16, 2026 /KestriaWire/ -- Rain around Ostara has increased the proportion of wheat deliveries requiring drying at Prairie Gold Grain Co-operative's local receiving site. Of the 61 wheat loads sampled during the past two days, 24 exceeded the standard moisture limit of 14 per cent. Accepted wet grain is being stored separately.

Lumen reduces prices on forty everyday food and cleaning products

Words by Daren Pell

13 Oct 2026

Lumen Home Retail has reduced prices on 40 products in its Everyday Basket range, effective today across all 42 stores and online. The reductions average 5.4% and cover items including porridge oats, dried beans, washing-up liquid and kitchen cloths. Pack sizes and product specifications remain the same.

A 1 kg bag of porridge oats now costs KRN 8.40, down from KRN 8.90, while a 500 ml bottle of washing-up liquid falls from KRN 6.20 to KRN 5.80. Shelf labels show the previous price alongside the new price to help customers compare.

Lower packaging costs and changes to delivery schedules have helped fund the reductions. Lumen has committed to hold the new prices until at least 31 December. The remaining 110 Everyday Basket products retain their existing prices. The company said the reductions were included in its current trading plans and did not alter its financial expectations for the year.

Val-Brume stores introduce clearer French labels across household essentials

Words by Elira Venn

6 Oct 2026

Lumen Home Retail has introduced clearer French-language shelf labels at its three Val-Brume stores. The change covers 2,300 household and grocery products, including cleaning supplies, bedding and cupboard staples. Product names, pack sizes and unit prices now appear together in a larger, consistent format.

The work follows an eight-week review with customers and store colleagues in Kestria's French-speaking region. Participants said that unit prices were sometimes difficult to locate and that several household product descriptions needed simpler wording. Printed guidance at service desks and online collection instructions have also been revised.

The project cost KRN 210,000, including translation, printing and staff training. It does not change product prices or the ranges stocked. Lumen will collect feedback at the three stores through November and check a sample of labels each week for accuracy. Customers can report unclear wording at any service desk or through the retailer's website.

Stock Check Confirms Grain Records Across Four Storage Sites

KESTREL BAY, Kestria, Oct. 22, 2026 /KestriaWire/ -- Prairie Gold Grain Co-operative has completed its autumn stock check at Amberford, Ostara, Kestrel Bay and Val-Brume. Measured stocks at the close of 21 October totalled 121,460 tonnes of wheat and 34,280 tonnes of oats. The figures include grain already allocated to customers but awaiting collection.

Staff compared bin measurements with receiving tickets, dispatch weights and recorded cleaning losses. The combined difference between measured grain and stock records was 0.08 per cent, within the co-operative's internal tolerance of 0.20 per cent. All four sites completed checks, and no unexplained difference required a customer allocation to be changed.

Routine temperature readings also found no storage parcel above the co-operative's action threshold of 20 degrees. Store teams continue to check grain condition and record aeration work. Customers requesting available volumes should contact the sales desk, as total physical stock includes committed grain and parcels held for further preparation.

Kestrel Bay Loading Repairs Restore Normal Grain Dispatch Capacity

OSTARA, Kestria, Oct. 6, 2026 /KestriaWire/ -- Prairie Gold Grain Co-operative has restored normal dispatch capacity at its Kestrel Bay store after replacing a worn bearing in the grain loading conveyor. The conveyor returned to service on 5 October following an inspection and an unloaded test. Grain receiving continued while the equipment was unavailable.

The interruption delayed nine customer collections carrying a combined 270 tonnes of wheat and oats. Six have now been completed, and revised collection times have been agreed for the remaining three. No grain was damaged, and the affected conveyor did not require any stored stock to be discarded.

The loading line is again operating at its normal rate of up to 90 tonnes an hour, subject to vehicle changes and sampling. Customers should use the collection time shown on their latest dispatch confirmation. Drivers arriving early must wait in the marked parking area until called to the loading point.

Competition clearance received for proposed Hearthmere Bakery acquisition

By Mara Fenwick

9 October 2026

Bramble Foods has received clearance from Kestria's competition authority for its proposed acquisition of Hearthmere Bakery. The KRN 24.6 million cash transaction was announced on 18 September. Clearance satisfies one of the principal conditions of the purchase agreement, with completion still subject to the remaining customary requirements.

The companies are now preparing final completion documents and arrangements for transferring ownership. Bramble Foods continues to expect the transaction to complete by the end of October. Hearthmere remains independently owned and managed until that process has concluded.

Plans announced in September to retain Hearthmere's name, Val-Brume production site and 86 employees remain in place. Initial work following completion would focus on financial reporting, purchasing procedures and customer service arrangements. Bramble Foods said there would be no immediate changes to Hearthmere's recipes or product packaging. A separate announcement will confirm completion and the date from which Hearthmere's results enter the group accounts.

Amberford bakery prepares new packing line for autumn commissioning

By Leonie Varnet

28 August 2026

Bramble Foods has completed the main installation work on a new packing line at its Amberford bakery. The KRN 8.4 million project replaces two older machines used for small cake packs and is scheduled to enter commissioning in October. Electrical checks and staff training will take place during September.

Once fully operational, the line is expected to increase the site's cake packing capacity by 18% and reduce film waste per pack by about 11%. These estimates will be checked during production trials. The bakery will continue supplying customers through its existing equipment while the new line is tested.

The project includes 14 additional permanent roles across production, maintenance and quality control. Recruitment has begun locally, with practical training provided on site. Bramble Foods said the investment supports demand for smaller packs without requiring an extension to the bakery building. Total spending remains within the approved project budget.

Lumen outlines Saltmarsh depot upgrade ahead of winter trading

Words by Elira Venn

23 Oct 2026

Lumen Home Retail will invest KRN 4.6 million in new sorting equipment and additional chilled holding space at its Saltmarsh distribution depot. Installation is scheduled to begin on 2 November and finish in stages by mid-December. The project forms part of the retailer's existing KRN 34 million annual investment budget.

The upgrade will add 320 chilled pallet spaces and replace two ageing conveyor sections used for household goods. Lumen expects the changes to reduce manual handling and give stores more flexibility when ordering fresh food. The depot currently supplies 27 of the company's 42 stores, including branches in Ostara and Val-Brume.

Work will take place in separate sections while normal deliveries continue. Lumen has leased temporary chilled storage for the installation period and scheduled staff training before each new section enters use. Eight maintenance and warehouse roles are being recruited. The company expects to assess delivery accuracy and equipment reliability after the upgraded sections have operated for eight weeks.

Lumen agrees new credit facility to support planned store investment

Words by Daren Pell

23 Sep 2026

Lumen Home Retail has signed a KRN 120 million revolving credit facility with Brackenmere Commercial Bank and Ternfold Lending. The facility matures in September 2030 and replaces a KRN 90 million agreement that was due to expire next year. It provides funds that Lumen can draw and repay as needed.

At signing, KRN 28 million was drawn under the new agreement to repay the outstanding balance on the previous facility. The remaining capacity is available for seasonal stock purchases and planned investment in stores and distribution equipment. No shares were issued as part of the financing.

Finance director Sella Morven said the agreement gave Lumen greater certainty over funding while retaining room for quieter trading periods. Interest is charged at a variable reference rate plus an agreed margin. The facility includes quarterly borrowing and interest-cover tests. Lumen met those requirements at signing and has not changed its full-year investment budget of KRN 34 million.

Posted: Monday, September 28, 2026
Posted by: Lucien Bréval

Oakhill Bakeries Group has revised its wholesale price list, increasing prices by an average of 3.2 per cent across its bread and roll range. The new list applies from today. Customers received four weeks' written notice, including a product-by-product schedule showing the changes.

The wholesale price of a standard 800g white loaf has risen from KRN 4.10 to KRN 4.23. A pack of six plain rolls has increased from KRN 3.60 to KRN 3.72. Prices for seven products, including selected sweet buns, remain unchanged.

Oakhill's contracted flour cost is 9.1 per cent higher than under its previous supply agreement. Packaging costs have also increased. Commercial manager Nerys Fennholt said savings from production and purchasing have absorbed part of the rise. Retailers set their own selling prices, and Oakhill's delivery threshold and small-order charge remain unchanged.

News release

Gas network ruling disallows unsupported maintenance costs

Published: 30 September 2026

The Kestria Energy Board has disallowed KRN 1.8 million of maintenance costs claimed by the Saltmarsh gas network operator. The ruling follows a review of expenditure for the year ended 30 June. The operator did not provide sufficient work records to support costs assigned to 23 maintenance jobs.

The disputed amount forms part of a KRN 41.6 million maintenance claim. The Board accepted KRN 39.8 million after checking invoices, inspection records and staff time entries. The disallowed costs cannot be recovered through regulated network charges. This decision does not alter the tariff currently shown on customer bills.

The ruling concerns evidence supporting expenditure. It makes no finding that the maintenance itself was unnecessary or that the network is unsafe. The operator must keep clearer records linking each charge to completed work. A summary of the assessment explains the evidence requirements and lists the categories of costs that were excluded.

News release

Board clarifies billing rules following household tariff reduction

Published: 17 September 2026

The Kestria Energy Board has issued billing guidance following the household electricity standing charge reduction on 15 September. The guidance addresses questions received from customers and suppliers about bills covering days on both sides of the change. It does not introduce another tariff change.

For a bill covering 1 to 30 September, suppliers must charge 14 days at KRN 0.84 and 16 days at KRN 0.79. The standing charge for that period is therefore KRN 24.40. Electricity used during the period remains subject to the unchanged unit rate of KRN 0.246 per kilowatt hour.

Customers using advance credit meters are also entitled to the lower standing charge from 15 September. Where a meter update has taken longer, suppliers must credit the difference. The Board has asked suppliers to keep records of these adjustments so its billing team can check that customers receive the full reduction.

Posted by: Mara Denholt

Oakhill Bakeries Group's new Kestrel Bay bakery began commercial production today, supplying plain rolls and breakfast buns to 38 local shops. Opening output is six tonnes a day against a designed daily capacity of 20 tonnes. Orders are being added in stages as production settles.

Posted: Monday, October 5, 2026
Posted by: Elin Veymar

Oakhill Bakeries Group has confirmed the closure of its Ostara bakery following consultation with employees. The decision affects 31 roles. The company considered proposals for shorter production weeks, a smaller product range and additional contract baking, but none provided enough regular work to cover the site's costs.

Nineteen employees have accepted roles elsewhere in the group: 11 at Amberford and eight at Kestrel Bay. Twelve employees remain at risk of redundancy and have received individual statements setting out their payments and support. Transfer offers include travel assistance for an initial six-month period.

The Ostara bakery remains in production while customer orders are transferred in stages. Staff have paid time for interviews and employment advice. Managing director Tessa Oakhill thanked employees for their proposals and said the decision reflects the building's operating costs and low utilisation, rather than the quality of their work.

Amberford packing trials meet quality targets ahead of production

By Leonie Varnet

16 October 2026

Bramble Foods has completed the initial commissioning trials for its new cake packing line at Amberford. Trial packs met the site's checks for seal strength, weight accuracy and product protection. The line is scheduled to begin regular customer production on 19 October, initially operating on one shift.

The KRN 8.4 million investment was outlined in August. All 14 additional permanent roles have now been filled, and operators have completed supervised training. Existing packing equipment will remain available during the early production period so that the bakery can maintain deliveries if adjustments are required.

Early trials indicate that the line can support the planned increase in capacity, but Bramble Foods will assess sustained output and packaging waste over a full month of production. The company expects to add a second shift as orders require. Final project spending remains within budget, including installation, training and a supply of essential spare parts.

Port publishes revised charges for empty container storage

Tomas Bellwick 29 Sep 2026

The Port of Kestrel Bay published a revised empty-container storage tariff today. Under the tariff now in force, the first five calendar days remain free. Storage from day six to day ten costs KRN 18 per standard container unit per day, compared with KRN 15 under the previous tariff.

The rate from day eleven is KRN 31 per unit per day, an increase of KRN 4. Loaded-container storage, vessel dues and rail handling charges are unchanged. Containers already in the empty yard before today remain subject to the previous rates for their current stay.

Empty containers occupied an average of 81 per cent of designated yard spaces during August. The revised charges follow a tariff review circulated to account holders in July. Customers can view the applicable rate and arrival date for each container in their account record, or request a written breakdown from the port billing team.

Repair work began at Berth Four today after an inspection found worn fittings along the outer quay edge. Corvel updates carton prices following higher board costs

By Ellis Dacre · September 30, 2026
Share: LinkedIn X Email

Corvel Packaging has increased base prices for newly quoted folding cartons by an average of 3.4 per cent from today. Individual changes range from 2.1 to 4.6 per cent, depending on board grade, carton weight and print requirements. Confirmed orders retain their agreed base prices.

The adjustment follows higher delivered board costs recorded during August and September. It applies to cartons produced at Amberford and does not change the base prices of trays or films. The energy surcharge remains separate at KRN 58 per tonne and is calculated using dispatch weight.

Get Corvel news in your inbox

Sign up for our monthly update on packaging prices, new products and sustainability. You can unsubscribe at any time.

Related: Corvel adds recycled content option for selected food trays

Revised quotations show the base price and estimated surcharge separately so customers can compare the full cost at a stated order quantity. Existing written quotations remain valid until their stated expiry dates. Account teams can review board grades or order sizes with customers, although any specification change still requires approval before production.

Ostara workshop helps manufacturers check labels before printing

Media centre · Elise Marvaux
21 September

Thirty-four staff from 22 food businesses attended a label checking workshop in Ostara, organised by the Food Manufacturers Federation of Kestria. The session focused on common errors that can be caught before packaging goes to print.

Participants worked through fictional product labels covering soups, baked goods and chilled meals. Exercises included checking ingredient order, matching declared weights to product specifications and making storage instructions easy to find.

Elise Marvaux, technical affairs manager, said: “A second check against the recipe and specification can prevent an expensive reprint. Staff need a clear process for recording who approved a label and which version was sent to the printer.”

The federation distributed a two-page checklist and a sample approval record. The materials reflect current requirements and identify matters still under consultation in the draft labelling guidance. French versions are available to members through the federation’s advice service in Val-Brume.

Wage talks open with focus on pay and training

Media centre · Devran Pell
9 September

Negotiations on Kestria’s next food manufacturing sector wage agreement opened in Saltmarsh today. The Food Manufacturers Federation of Kestria is representing 63 employers covered by the agreement, alongside representatives of the Food Production Workers Union.

The opening meeting covered basic pay, shift allowances and access to paid training. The current agreement provides a minimum hourly rate of KRN 14.20 for adult production workers at participating businesses.

Devran Pell, employment relations manager, said: “We want an agreement that improves pay and helps factories retain skilled people. Employers also need to understand the full cost, including allowances, before they can make a firm commitment.”

Both negotiating teams exchanged evidence on vacancies, staff turnover and business costs. No pay settlement was reached at the opening meeting. The federation has asked participating employers to check their payroll information so that further discussions use consistent figures for hours, grades and shift patterns.

Posted: Friday, October 16, 2026
Posted by: Mara Denholt

Oakhill Bakeries Group reduced bread production waste to 2.8 per cent of baked weight in September, down from 3.6 per cent in June. The comparison covers Amberford, Saltmarsh and Ostara, which operated during both months. It excludes the new Kestrel Bay bakery.

The measure includes misshapen loaves, products damaged during packing and bread rejected during quality checks. It does not include unsold goods returned by shops, which Oakhill records separately. Production waste across the three sites fell from 54 tonnes in June to 43 tonnes in September.

Teams adjusted dough portion settings, improved checks at shift changes and replaced worn guides on two packing lines. Operations director Brenna Halewick said these small changes reduced avoidable losses without relaxing product standards. Site teams review the figures weekly, using weighing records and production totals to identify where further checks are needed.

Posted: Thursday, August 27, 2026
Posted by: Lucien Bréval

Oakhill Bakeries Group has introduced a single delivery charge for small shop orders across its existing delivery network in Kestria. Orders below KRN 240 now carry a KRN 12 charge. Orders at or above that value receive delivery without a separate fee.

The change replaces six local charging arrangements that had developed as delivery routes expanded. Product prices are unchanged. Customers received individual notices and examples showing how the revised charge applies to their usual orders, including mixed orders of bread, rolls and sweet bakery products.

The same threshold applies in Saltmarsh, Kestrel Bay, Ostara, Amberford and Val-Brume. Customers can combine products on one order to reach it. Commercial manager Nerys Fennholt said the simpler arrangement makes invoices easier to check and helps shopkeepers compare the cost of placing several small orders with one larger delivery.

News release

Amberford electricity connection delays prompt formal improvement notice

Published: 6 October 2026

The Kestria Energy Board has issued a formal improvement notice to the Amberford electricity network operator after an audit found repeated delays in providing connection quotations. Of 160 complete applications examined, 47 had not received a quotation within the required 15 working days.

The applications covered small shops, workshops and housing developments. The longest recorded wait was 38 working days. The operator attributed the backlog to vacancies and incomplete internal handovers. The Board found that these problems did not remove its obligation to meet the published service standard.

The notice requires weekly reporting of outstanding quotations and a named contact for every affected applicant. It also requires the operator to separate applications awaiting customer information from those delayed within its own teams. The notice imposes no financial penalty. Applicants can ask the operator for a written explanation of their case and use the Board's complaints route if it remains unresolved.

News release

Ostara industrial gas restrictions lifted after equipment repairs

Published: 29 September 2026

Supply restrictions on the East Ostara industrial gas branch have been lifted following repairs to a pressure regulator. The Kestria Energy Board confirmed the change after reviewing test records supplied by the network operator. The branch has returned to its normal available capacity of 92 megawatt hours per hour.

The restrictions affected 14 sites with interruptible supply agreements from 22 September. The operator recorded a total requested reduction of 16 megawatt hours per hour during the restriction period. It has reported no interruption to household supplies and no loss of gas containment associated with the equipment fault.

Affected businesses have received individual notices cancelling their temporary limits. The Board has requested maintenance records and an explanation of how the fault developed. This review is separate from the decision to restore capacity. Businesses disputing a charge connected with the restriction should first use their supplier's complaints process and retain their meter records.

Bramble Foods completes acquisition of Hearthmere Bakery in Val-Brume

By Mara Fenwick

21 October 2026

Bramble Foods today completed its acquisition of Hearthmere Bakery for KRN 24.6 million in cash. All remaining completion conditions have been satisfied following competition clearance announced on 9 October. Hearthmere's financial results will be included in Bramble Foods' group accounts from today.

The Val-Brume business makes crispbreads and seeded biscuits and employs 86 people. Its name, production site and workforce have been retained. Customers will continue to place orders through their existing contacts, and current supply agreements remain in effect. Product recipes and packaging are unchanged at completion.

The purchase was funded through a combination of available cash and drawings under Bramble Foods' existing borrowing facilities. During the first three months of ownership, work will concentrate on reporting systems, supplier arrangements and planning for future orders. Bramble Foods expects a small contribution to group revenue for the remainder of 2026 and will provide further detail with its full-year results.

Third quarter sales rise as bakery demand remains steady

By Mara Fenwick

19 October 2026

Bramble Foods recorded revenue of KRN 219.4 million for the three months ended 30 September 2026, an increase of 4.8% compared with the same quarter last year. Revenue for the first nine months reached KRN 648.0 million. Third-quarter sales volumes grew by 1.3%, supported by steady bread demand and higher cracker sales.

Trading remained strongest in Saltmarsh and Amberford, while orders from smaller shops were more variable. The new oat cracker range began shipping near the quarter end and made only a small contribution. Wholesale price changes introduced on 1 October had no effect on the reported quarter.

The board's full-year operating profit expectations remain unchanged. Regular production on Amberford's new packing line began today, with performance monitoring under way. The proposed Hearthmere Bakery acquisition has received competition clearance but has not yet completed. Its trading is therefore excluded from these figures, and completion remains expected by the end of October.

September figures show shorter queues at freight gates

Mara Venn 5 Oct 2026

Average lorry turnaround time at the Port of Kestrel Bay fell to 39 minutes in September, compared with 43 minutes in July. The monthly figure covers 31,480 completed visits and includes time spent waiting inside the terminal. Visits cancelled before arrival are excluded.

The port handled 82,900 standard container units during September. This was 2.4 per cent above the same month last year, despite the wind stoppage on 3 September and the reduced working length at Berth Four. Rail accounted for 29 per cent of containers leaving the port by land.

Gate staff recorded fewer arrivals without bookings after hauliers began receiving an additional booking reminder in August. Unbooked arrivals fell from 412 in August to 267 in September. The authority asks drivers to check the container release status before travelling, as a gate booking alone does not confirm that cargo is ready for collection.

Port publishes revised charges for empty container storage

Tomas Bellwick 29 Sep 2026

The Port of Kestrel Bay published a revised empty-container storage tariff today. Under the tariff now in force, the first five calendar days remain free. Storage from day six to day ten costs KRN 18 per standard container unit per day, compared with KRN 15 under the previous tariff.

The rate from day eleven is KRN 31 per unit per day, an increase of KRN 4. Loaded-container storage, vessel dues and rail handling charges are unchanged. Containers already in the empty yard before today remain subject to the previous rates for their current stay.

Empty containers occupied an average of 81 per cent of designated yard spaces during August. The revised charges follow a tariff review circulated to account holders in July. Customers can view the applicable rate and arrival date for each container in their account record, or request a written breakdown from the port billing team.

Maintenance vacancies remain hardest to fill in autumn survey

Media centre · Tomas Bellan
9 October

Maintenance roles remain the hardest vacancies for food manufacturers to fill, according to a staffing survey released today by the Food Manufacturers Federation of Kestria. Seventy-six member businesses responded between 22 September and 2 October.

Among the 49 respondents recruiting during that period, 29 reported difficulty hiring maintenance staff. Twenty-one reported difficulty recruiting machine operators. Businesses could select more than one role, so the figures do not represent separate groups of employers.

Tomas Bellan, research manager, said: “Employers described a shortage of applicants with experience of fault finding and routine equipment care. Several businesses in Kestrel Bay said vacancies had increased their reliance on external repair services.”

Thirty-two respondents said they had increased internal training during the previous six months. The federation is using the findings in discussions with training providers in Amberford and Ostara. The survey did not measure the effect of the proposed wage settlement announced this week.

Manufacturers seek simpler rules for proposed packaging levy

Media centre · Mara Vennick
28 August

The Food Manufacturers Federation of Kestria has called for changes to a proposed packaging levy, saying the current draft would require manufacturers to report the same material more than once.

In its submission to the Ministry of Revenue, the federation supports charging by packaging weight but asks for a single reporting return. The proposal sets a rate of KRN 0.18 per kilogram for certain packaging materials.

A review of records from 26 member businesses found that 19 would need to change their stock systems under the draft rules. Smaller manufacturers estimated an average initial cost of KRN 8,400, excluding staff time.

Mara Vennick, the federation’s policy director, said: “Members need clear definitions and a practical way to submit figures. One return, with worked examples, would help businesses meet the rules and make the information easier to check.”

Oakhill Bakeries Group has launched three seasonal products while retaining the wholesale price of its standard 800g white loaf at KRN 4.23. The new range consists of a spiced apple bun, a pear-filled pastry and a round oat loaf, available to order from today.

Posted: Monday, October 5, 2026
Posted by: Elin Veymar

Oakhill Bakeries Group has confirmed the closure of its Ostara bakery following consultation with employees. The decision affects 31 roles. The company considered proposals for shorter production weeks, a smaller product range and additional contract baking, but none provided enough regular work to cover the site's costs.

Nineteen employees have accepted roles elsewhere in the group: 11 at Amberford and eight at Kestrel Bay. Twelve employees remain at risk of redundancy and have received individual statements setting out their payments and support. Transfer offers include travel assistance for an initial six-month period.

The Ostara bakery remains in production while customer orders are transferred in stages. Staff have paid time for interviews and employment advice. Managing director Tessa Oakhill thanked employees for their proposals and said the decision reflects the building's operating costs and low utilisation, rather than the quality of their work.

Exchange extends afternoon trading for all agricultural futures

Notice No. 2026/341 · Category: Contracts

Date of issue: 28.09.2026 · Effective: 12.10.2026

Ostara Commodities Exchange has extended its regular trading session by 30 minutes. From today, wheat, oat and rapeseed futures trade from 08:30 to 16:30, using the exchange clock in Ostara. The opening time is unchanged. Members can enter orders during the pre-opening period from 08:15.

The daily settlement calculation now uses eligible trading activity between 16:20 and 16:30. Where activity is insufficient, the exchange applies its existing rules for assessing bids, offers and related contract months. The longer session responds to requests from members handling afternoon warehouse confirmations in Amberford and freight arrangements through Kestrel Bay.

Orders marked to expire at the end of the trading day now remain active until 16:30 unless cancelled or filled. Orders carrying a specific expiry time retain that instruction. Members should review automated schedules and staffing arrangements. The extension does not alter delivery notice deadlines, collateral payment deadlines or the opening hours of approved warehouses.

Amberford warehouse approved for additional wheat delivery capacity

Notice No. 2026/334 · Category: Trading hours

Date of issue: 14.09.2026 · Effective: 21.09.2026

Ostara Commodities Exchange has approved a further 12,000 tonnes of wheat storage at the Merebank warehouse in Amberford. The additional capacity is eligible for exchange delivery from today. Approval follows checks of weighing equipment, sampling facilities, stock records and the separation of grain held for different owners.

The extension brings Merebank's approved wheat capacity to 30,000 tonnes. It does not add oat or rapeseed storage to the site's approval. Wheat placed into exchange delivery must meet the existing contract standards, including a maximum moisture content of 14.5 per cent. Warehouse approval does not replace the inspection required for each delivery lot.

Members arranging delivery should confirm available space directly with the warehouse before submitting a notice. The exchange's register now shows the additional capacity and the site's receiving hours. Merebank must report eligible stocks each trading day and notify the exchange immediately if equipment faults, access restrictions or stock discrepancies affect its ability to receive or release grain.

News release

Board approves lower overnight network charge for industry

Published: 16 October 2026

The Kestria Energy Board has approved a lower overnight electricity network charge for eligible industrial connections in Kestrel Bay. From today, the charge for electricity carried between midnight and 05:00 is KRN 0.018 per kilowatt hour, down from KRN 0.023. Other network rates remain unchanged.

The decision covers 38 connections with meters that record consumption in half-hour periods. Network evidence showed spare capacity during the overnight window and lower costs for carrying additional demand at those times. The Board accepted the proposed reduction after checking the operator's demand records and allocation of costs.

A qualifying site using 100,000 kilowatt hours entirely within the overnight window pays KRN 500 less in network charges for that consumption. This is only one part of its electricity bill. Energy supply prices, capacity charges and other applicable items are separate. Suppliers must identify the revised network rate clearly in their billing calculations.

Val-Brume office expands access to energy billing advice

Published: 14 October 2026

The Kestria Energy Board's Val-Brume office has introduced an additional weekly session for customers seeking help with electricity and gas bills. The service provides advice in French and English. It covers tariff explanations, estimated readings, disputed charges and the steps involved in making a formal complaint.

The additional session follows a rise in local enquiries from 86 in July to 129 in September. Most concerned estimated bills and difficulties obtaining account corrections. Customers can bring a recent bill, relevant meter readings and copies of messages already exchanged with their supplier. There is no charge for the service.

Staff can explain the rules and help customers identify the information needed to pursue a case. They cannot change a meter reading or promise a particular complaint outcome during an advice session. The office's published service information includes accessible appointment options and arrangements for customers who need someone to speak on their behalf.

Berth Four fully reopens after quay repairs finish

Nina Halden 15 Oct 2026

Berth Four returned to its full working length of 305 metres today after the final repaired section passed inspection. Work began on 2 September and covered six mooring bollards, eight fenders and the concrete around the bollard foundations. The temporary fencing has been removed.

The completed work cost KRN 8.1 million against an allocation of KRN 8.4 million. The total includes engineering inspections, load tests and disposal of removed materials. Engineers signed off the final three bollards yesterday, and terminal staff completed checks of lighting and quay access before reopening the section.

Both container services temporarily reassigned to Berth Two are now back at Berth Four. Shipping agents have received the updated berth plan. The authority has also closed the temporary pedestrian diversion behind the works. Port users can use the usual marked walkway, while access to the quay edge remains restricted to authorised staff.

September figures show shorter queues at freight gates

Mara Venn 5 Oct 2026

Average lorry turnaround time at the Port of Kestrel Bay fell to 39 minutes in September, compared with 43 minutes in July. The monthly figure covers 31,480 completed visits and includes time spent waiting inside the terminal. Visits cancelled before arrival are excluded.

The port handled 82,900 standard container units during September. This was 2.4 per cent above the same month last year, despite the wind stoppage on 3 September and the reduced working length at Berth Four. Rail accounted for 29 per cent of containers leaving the port by land.

Gate staff recorded fewer arrivals without bookings after hauliers began receiving an additional booking reminder in August. Unbooked arrivals fell from 412 in August to 267 in September. The authority asks drivers to check the container release status before travelling, as a gate booking alone does not confirm that cargo is ready for collection.

Annual report records faster action on unpaid pension contributions

Written by Mara Ellwick

The Pensions Oversight Authority's annual report, published today, records KRN 6.8 million in overdue employer contributions recovered following its intervention during the year ended 31 March 2026. The payments reached 73 workplace pension plans covering 18,420 members. Recoveries totalled KRN 5.1 million in the previous reporting year.

The median time from opening a contribution case to securing payment fell from 47 to 34 working days. These figures cover completed cases; they do not include money still being pursued at the year end.

Operating expenditure was KRN 24.6 million against a budget of KRN 25.2 million. The report includes audited accounts, service measures and a breakdown of complaints about the Authority. Priorities for the current year include earlier checks on missed payments and clearer guidance for employers running smaller workplace plans.

Workplace pension funding improves in second quarter review

Written by Mara Ellwick

The Pensions Oversight Authority estimates that workplace pension plans promising a set retirement income held assets equal to 104 per cent of their liabilities at the end of June. This compares with 102 per cent at the end of March. The review covers 842 plans across Kestria, with combined assets of KRN 186 billion.

The improvement mainly reflects higher investment income and employer contributions. Funding remains uneven: 176 plans held less than the estimated amount needed to meet their promises. A national average does not show whether an individual plan can pay every benefit when it falls due.

Employers and trustees should continue making scheduled payments and reviewing their funding assumptions. The figures are estimates based on quarterly returns, rather than full valuations of every plan. The Authority has published regional tables, including separate results for Saltmarsh, Kestrel Bay, Ostara, Amberford and Val-Brume.

Corvel expands returnable pallet scheme after Saltmarsh customer trial

By Nadia Pell · October 21, 2026
Share: LinkedIn X Email

Corvel Packaging has expanded its returnable pallet scheme to regular delivery routes serving Amberford and Val-Brume. The scheme follows a 12-week trial with eight food producers in Saltmarsh. Participating customers returned 438 of the 480 pallets issued during the trial.

Of the returned pallets, 421 passed inspection for reuse and 17 required repair. Corvel records each pallet by reference number and collects empty pallets during an agreed delivery visit. The scheme uses a refundable deposit of KRN 85 per pallet, shown separately from packaging and transport charges.

Kestrel Bay film line returns after planned maintenance

By Mara Venn · October 8, 2026
Share: LinkedIn X Email

Corvel Packaging has returned its second film line at Kestrel Bay to normal production following a four-day maintenance shutdown. Work included replacing heater controls, checking winding equipment and servicing the cooling system. The line produces sealing films for prepared-food trays.

Operators completed restart checks on three film thicknesses before releasing production. Tests covered thickness variation, roll tension and seal performance against approved tray samples. All three trial batches met their existing specifications. The work has not changed the materials used or the approved uses of the films.

Federation publishes costing guide for proposed wage agreement

Media centre · Devran Pell
12 October

The Food Manufacturers Federation of Kestria has published a costing guide to help participating employers assess the proposed sector wage agreement. The guide accompanies the settlement terms circulated on 7 October.

Worked examples cover basic pay, shift allowances and paid training time. For an employee working 38 paid hours a week at the adult production minimum, the proposed hourly increase of KRN 0.65 would add KRN 24.70 to weekly basic pay.

The guide explains that this figure excludes overtime, allowances and employer contributions. It also asks businesses to account for training cover where production duties need to be reassigned during an employee’s eight annual paid training hours.

Devran Pell, employment relations manager, said: “Employers need to assess the whole agreement using their own staffing patterns. These examples provide a common starting point.” The proposal remains subject to approval, and the guide does not replace the full settlement document or individual employment contracts.

Packaging levy revision removes duplicate reporting for manufacturers

Media centre · Mara Vennick
17 September

The Food Manufacturers Federation of Kestria has welcomed a revised packaging levy proposal published today by the Ministry of Revenue. The revision provides for one reporting return and removes a provision that could have counted some packaging twice.

The proposed rate remains KRN 0.18 per kilogram for the materials covered. The ministry has also added examples showing how manufacturers should record packaging purchased through wholesalers and packaging transferred between factories.

Mara Vennick, policy director, said: “These changes address a practical problem raised in our submission. Businesses can now assess the proposal with a clearer understanding of what they would need to report.”

The federation continues to seek clarification on reusable transport containers and the treatment of returned goods. It has asked members to submit examples with weights and purchase records. The levy remains a proposal, and the federation advises businesses to distinguish the draft requirements from their existing reporting duties.

Trading resumes after morning interruption to order entry

Notice No. 2026/362 · Category: Trading hours

Date of issue: 08.10.2026 · Effective: 15.10.2026

Trading in wheat, oat and rapeseed futures resumed at 10:05 today after an interruption to the exchange's order entry service. Ostara Commodities Exchange suspended matching at 09:12 when monitoring identified delays in order acknowledgements. A ten-minute period for members to review and cancel orders preceded the reopening.

Trades completed before the suspension remain valid. Orders that had been accepted and remained unfilled were retained with their original priority. Messages that did not receive an acceptance acknowledgement were not added to the order book. Members were asked to reconcile their records against the exchange's order and trade reports before entering replacement instructions.

Technical staff traced the interruption to a fault in a message queue and moved the service to reserve equipment. The regular 16:30 closing time remains in place. Clearing and warehouse reporting services continued to operate during the interruption. The exchange is reviewing system records and member reports to establish why the fault was not resolved automatically.

Wheat margin requirements rise after increased market volatility

Notice No. 2026/348 · Category: Margins

Date of issue: 05.10.2026 · Effective: 12.10.2026

Ostara Commodities Exchange has raised the initial margin for wheat futures from KRN 1,600 to KRN 1,900 per contract. The maintenance margin increases from KRN 1,300 to KRN 1,550. The new requirements apply to all listed wheat months at today's clearing calculation, including positions opened before the announcement.

The adjustment reflects larger daily price movements and a greater concentration of positions in the nearest delivery month. Over the past five sessions, the average wheat price range was KRN 17 per tonne. Each contract covers 20 tonnes. Clearing members must provide any additional collateral by 09:00 on the next trading day. Members may apply higher requirements to their own clients under their account agreements. News release

Quarterly report records fewer unresolved energy billing complaints

Published: 20 October 2026

The Kestria Energy Board has published its complaints report for July to September. It received 642 electricity and gas complaints during the quarter, compared with 689 in the preceding quarter. There were 118 unresolved cases at the end of September, down from 151 at the end of June.

Billing accounted for 61 per cent of new complaints. The most common issues were estimated consumption, delayed corrections and unclear account balances. Connection delays accounted for a further 17 per cent. The figures cover cases brought to the Board after customers had first raised the matter with their supplier or network operator.

The median time taken to close a case was 19 working days, compared with 23 in the preceding quarter. The Board cautions that a closed case does not always mean a complaint was upheld. Its tables distinguish corrections, explanations, withdrawn cases and formal findings so readers can see how complaints were resolved.

News release

Gas network ruling disallows unsupported maintenance costs

Published: 30 September 2026

The Kestria Energy Board has disallowed KRN 1.8 million of maintenance costs claimed by the Saltmarsh gas network operator. The ruling follows a review of expenditure for the year ended 30 June. The operator did not provide sufficient work records to support costs assigned to 23 maintenance jobs.

The disputed amount forms part of a KRN 41.6 million maintenance claim. The Board accepted KRN 39.8 million after checking invoices, inspection records and staff time entries. The disallowed costs cannot be recovered through regulated network charges. This decision does not alter the tariff currently shown on customer bills.

The ruling concerns evidence supporting expenditure. It makes no finding that the maintenance itself was unnecessary or that the network is unsafe. The operator must keep clearer records linking each charge to completed work. A summary of the assessment explains the evidence requirements and lists the categories of costs that were excluded.
