Workshop report identifies recurring questions from accounts preparers

Last modified 7 October 2026 · 2 minute read

The Accounting Standards Council of Kestria has published a report on its four autumn workshops. A total of 163 people attended sessions in Saltmarsh, Kestrel Bay, Ostara and Val-Brume between 10 September and 1 October.

Questions informing future support

Participants submitted 58 questions before the sessions and raised further examples during discussion. Staff grouped the questions by topic, with revenue recognition and repair provisions accounting for just over half of the advance submissions.

  • Evidence supporting repair estimates
  • Revenue from partly completed deliveries
  • Choosing useful accounting policy information
  • Explaining changes in estimates

The report summarises recurring difficulties and includes six examples drawn from the sessions, with company details replaced by invented facts. It explains the standards in force during the workshops. The revenue amendments issued on 6 October are available separately. Staff will use the findings when proposing next year's educational programme; the report itself introduces no accounting requirements.

Council seeks views on clearer supplier finance disclosures

Last modified 19 August 2026 · 2 minute read

The Accounting Standards Council of Kestria has published proposed amendments to Kestrian Accounting Standard 14, Cash Flows and Financing. The proposals would require companies to explain arrangements under which a finance provider pays suppliers and the company later pays that provider.

Information proposed

The draft would introduce a single note showing the size and main terms of these arrangements. Companies would retain responsibility for deciding how the related liabilities and cash flows are classified under existing requirements.

  • Opening and closing liability balances
  • Amounts already paid to suppliers
  • Ranges of payment due dates
  • Significant changes without cash movements

Comments are invited by 30 September 2026. The Council particularly welcomes examples from manufacturers and wholesalers in Amberford and Ostara. Its initial proposal is for annual periods beginning on or after 1 January 2028, with early application permitted. The final requirements and transition arrangements will depend on the evidence received.

Revenue Service reports progress on sales tax refunds

Date: 08/10/2026

The Kestria Revenue Service processed 92 per cent of complete sales tax refund claims within 15 working days during September. This compares with 86 per cent in August. September payments totalled KRN 18.4 million across 1,760 claims, including claims from manufacturers, wholesalers and building contractors.

The improvement followed the reassignment of six processing staff to the refund team in Ostara. Claims requiring further checks are excluded from the 15-day measure while the service waits for requested information. The published figures include both the number of claims awaiting checks and the reasons for those checks.

At the end of September, 214 claims were awaiting invoices, bank account confirmation or an explanation of unusually large purchases. Businesses can check progress through their tax account. Sending the same claim again can delay processing because staff must establish whether it is a duplicate. A business should instead reply to the information request using its existing claim reference.

Payroll filing service restored after morning access problems

Date: 10/09/2026

Access to the Kestria Revenue Service payroll filing service was restored at 11.40 am today following a technical fault. The interruption began at 8.15 am and affected employers trying to open or submit payroll tax returns. Corporate tax and sales tax filing remained available.

The fault interrupted the connection between the sign-in page and payroll records. Technical checks found no evidence that employer or employee information had been lost or disclosed. Returns submitted before the interruption remain recorded, and employers do not need to send those returns again.

Employers who saw an error message during submission should check their filing history for a receipt number. If no receipt appears, they should reopen the saved return and submit it. The service logged 186 reports from employers, including businesses in Amberford and Kestrel Bay. Anyone still unable to file should contact the payroll support team and quote the message shown on screen.

Bracken Grid Bond Rating Holds After Amberford Storm Disruption

By Tomas Arven and Mara Vellin
October 9, 2026

Northstar Credit Analytics has maintained Bracken Grid's BBB senior unsecured bond rating and stable outlook following the 6 October storm in the Amberford district. The storm damaged overhead lines and interrupted supplies to 74,000 connections. By the evening of 8 October, the company had restored power to all but 1,900 affected connections.

Bracken Grid's preliminary estimate places repair costs at KRN 18 million to KRN 24 million. Northstar has assumed the full upper estimate in its initial assessment without relying on insurance receipts. The company had KRN 72 million in cash and KRN 110 million of undrawn committed facilities at the end of September.

These resources should allow repairs to proceed without materially weakening liquidity. The rating also allows for occasional weather-related disruption. Northstar will review the final repair bill, compensation payments and any changes to planned maintenance. Costs substantially above the current estimate, or evidence of wider network weaknesses, could alter the assessment.

Ostara Rental Housing Outlook Remains Stable Despite Higher Maintenance Spending

By Mara Vellin and Dario Selven
October 8, 2026

Northstar Credit Analytics has maintained a stable sector outlook for rated rental housing companies operating in Ostara. High occupancy and steady rent collection continue to support earnings, although repairs and borrowing costs are absorbing more cash. The assessment covers four issuers with a combined 28,400 homes.

Average occupancy stood at 97.4% at the end of August, compared with 97.1% a year earlier. Rent arrears remained modest at 1.8% of annual billed rent. Maintenance spending rose 8%, led by roof repairs and heating replacements. Fixed interest rates apply to 76% of the sample's debt, limiting the immediate effect of higher financing costs.

Northstar expects most issuers to fund routine repairs from rental income while keeping development programmes within committed borrowing limits. Ratings could come under pressure where large construction projects coincide with debt maturities. The stable sector outlook assumes occupancy remains above 96% and companies retain enough accessible funding to meet twelve months of planned spending.

Kestrian Food Producers Maintain Stable Outlook as Input Costs Ease

9 October 2026 | Written by Céline Arvane

Meridian Ratings has maintained a stable outlook for Kestria’s packaged food sector. Lower grain and container costs are helping producers rebuild margins, although household spending remains subdued. Across six rated companies, average operating margins increased to 11.2% in the first half of 2026 from 10.4% a year earlier.

Sales volumes rose just 0.8%, with stronger demand for basic products offset by weaker purchases of premium lines. Producers supplying retailers in Saltmarsh and Amberford reported increased use of promotions. Meridian expects price competition to limit how much of the recent cost relief companies retain.

The sector’s median net debt stood at 2.4 times operating profit before depreciation at June. Most rated producers have sufficient cash and committed facilities for planned investment over the next year. Debt-funded acquisitions or prolonged discounting would create greater pressure than the modest volume growth currently assumed in Meridian’s forecasts.

Meridian Rates Saltmarsh Waterworks Bond in Line With Issuer Rating

10 September 2026 | Written by Mara Ternell

Meridian Ratings has assigned an A minus rating to Saltmarsh Waterworks’ proposed KRN 180 million senior unsecured bond. The issue rating matches the company’s long-term issuer rating, which remains A minus with a stable outlook. The bond is expected to mature in September 2033.

The company intends to use KRN 120 million of the proceeds to repay a bank loan due in February 2027. The balance will fund pipe replacement and treatment equipment within its existing investment programme. The transaction would extend debt maturities while leaving total borrowing within Meridian’s previous forecasts.

The proposed bonds will rank equally with the company’s other senior unsecured obligations. Meridian’s assessment assumes that the final terms are consistent with the draft documents reviewed. Cost overruns or a material increase in borrowing beyond the current programme could weaken financial headroom, but neither is included in the base forecast.

Ostara depot changes cut damaged produce deliveries by nearly a quarter

8 October 2026Idris Weller, Corporate Affairs

GreenBasket Supermarkets has reduced damaged fruit and vegetable deliveries from its Ostara depot by 24 per cent following changes to packing and loading. The result compares damage recorded per thousand crates during July to September with the same three months of 2025.

The depot supplies 68 stores and handles about 410,000 produce crates each month. Changes included shallower crates for soft fruit, separate loading positions for heavier root vegetables and temperature checks at each loading bay. GreenBasket spent KRN 1.7 million on equipment and training for the work.

Depot manager Brenna Holt said staff had recorded where damage occurred before changing handling routines. The measured reduction represents approximately 7,800 fewer damaged crates over the quarter. Produce rejected by stores remains subject to the same quality checks, and items suitable for sale are assessed separately from stock that must be discarded.

GreenBasket recalls selected oat biscuits after incorrect allergen labelling

9 September 2026Sofia Merrow, Corporate Affairs

GreenBasket Supermarkets is recalling its 250-gram Honeyfield Oat Biscuits with batch code HB0902 and a best-before date of 18 February 2027. The affected packs contain milk, which is missing from the allergen statement. They are unsuitable for people with a milk allergy.

The biscuits were sold in 87 GreenBasket stores across Kestria between 3 and 8 September. Customers with a milk allergy should not eat them. Anyone who bought an affected pack can return it to any GreenBasket store for a full refund without a receipt. Other batch codes are not included in this recall.

GreenBasket identified the error during a packaging check yesterday and removed the affected stock from sale that evening. Recall notices are displayed in the relevant stores and on the customer website. Product safety manager Orla Venn said the company had received no reports of illness linked to the affected batch.

Share: LinkedIn X Email

Corvel Packaging has issued evidence sheets for 18 uncoated carton specifications supplied from Amberford. Each sheet identifies the board grade, coatings, inks and adhesives covered by the assessment. It also explains the conditions attached to the company's recycling statements.

Ostara tray plant cuts trim waste through tooling changes

By Tobin Merrow · September 29, 2026
Share: LinkedIn X Email

Corvel Packaging's Ostara plant has reduced trim waste on two chilled-food tray lines following changes to cutting tools and sheet positioning. Across eight weeks of measured production, trim represented 13.1 per cent of material fed into the lines, down from 16.4 per cent during the preceding eight weeks.

The comparison covers the same four tray designs and excludes trial runs. Staff adjusted the spacing between tray shapes and replaced worn cutting edges. The plant used 18 tonnes less sheet material than it would have used at the earlier trim rate for the recorded volume.

Tray dimensions, sealing surfaces and approved material specifications are unchanged. Clean trim from these lines is separated for controlled reprocessing, subject to the requirements of each product specification. Corvel is reporting the reduction as a material efficiency measure; it has not calculated a carbon saving from the work.

Kestrel Bay Loading Repairs Restore Normal Grain Dispatch Capacity

OSTARA, Kestria, Oct. 6, 2026 /KestriaWire/ -- Prairie Gold Grain Co-operative has restored normal dispatch capacity at its Kestrel Bay store after replacing a worn bearing in the grain loading conveyor. The conveyor returned to service on 5 October following an inspection and an unloaded test. Grain receiving continued while the equipment was unavailable.

The interruption delayed nine customer collections carrying a combined 270 tonnes of wheat and oats. Six have now been completed, and revised collection times have been agreed for the remaining three. No grain was damaged, and the affected conveyor did not require any stored stock to be discarded.

The loading line is again operating at its normal rate of up to 90 tonnes an hour, subject to vehicle changes and sampling. Customers should use the collection time shown on their latest dispatch confirmation. Drivers arriving early must wait in the marked parking area until called to the loading point.

Early Wheat Samples Show Firm Protein And Low Moisture

OSTARA, Kestria, Sept. 7, 2026 /KestriaWire/ -- The first new-season quality report from Prairie Gold Grain Co-operative shows average wheat protein of 12.6 per cent and average moisture of 13.2 per cent. The report covers 186 accepted loads, representing 5,920 tonnes delivered to the Amberford and Ostara receiving sites by 6 September.

Average wheat test weight was 78.4 kilogrammes per hectolitre. These results support the sale of several parcels for milling, although each customer contract has its own requirements. The samples mainly represent earlier-harvested fields and should not be treated as a measure of the whole crop.

Oat deliveries remain limited, with 740 tonnes accepted so far. Members can request the test results for their own loads through the receiving office. Any request for a second test must identify the delivery ticket, allowing staff to locate the sealed sample retained from that load.

Val-Brume stores introduce clearer French labels across household essentials

6 Oct 2026

Lumen Home Retail has introduced clearer French-language shelf labels at its three Val-Brume stores. The change covers 2,300 household and grocery products, including cleaning supplies, bedding and cupboard staples. Product names, pack sizes and unit prices now appear together in a larger, consistent format.

The work follows an eight-week review with customers and store colleagues in Kestria's French-speaking region. Participants said that unit prices were sometimes difficult to locate and that several household product descriptions needed simpler wording. Printed guidance at service desks and online collection instructions have also been revised.

The project cost KRN 210,000, including translation, printing and staff training. It does not change product prices or the ranges stocked. Lumen will collect feedback at the three stores through November and check a sample of labels each week for accuracy. Customers can report unclear wording at any service desk or through the retailer's website.

New Ostara bakery agreement brings daily deliveries to more stores

16 Sep 2026

Lumen Home Retail has signed a three-year supply agreement with Hearthmere Baking, a family-owned producer based in Ostara. From 21 September, the bakery will supply bread and rolls to 14 Lumen stores, extending an existing arrangement covering six branches. The agreement is worth an estimated KRN 7.2 million over its term.

Hearthmere has installed an additional oven and created nine production and packing jobs to support the wider service. Deliveries will reach stores before opening on six mornings each week. The range includes a small sliced loaf developed after customers asked for more choices suited to smaller households.

Lumen will provide weekly order forecasts and pay agreed invoices within 21 days. Both businesses will review unsold quantities each month, with the aim of reducing surplus without leaving shelves empty late in the day. Existing bakery suppliers will continue serving Lumen stores outside the expanded delivery area.

By Mara Fenwick

9 October 2026

Bramble Foods has received clearance from Kestria's competition authority for its proposed acquisition of Hearthmere Bakery. The KRN 24.6 million cash transaction was announced on 18 September. Amberford bakery prepares new packing line for autumn commissioning

By Leonie Varnet

28 August 2026

Bramble Foods has completed the main installation work on a new packing line at its Amberford bakery. The KRN 8.4 million project replaces two older machines used for small cake packs and is scheduled to enter commissioning in October. Electrical checks and staff training will take place during September.

Once fully operational, the line is expected to increase the site's cake packing capacity by 18% and reduce film waste per pack by about 11%. These estimates will be checked during production trials. The bakery will continue supplying customers through its existing equipment while the new line is tested.

The project includes 14 additional permanent roles across production, maintenance and quality control. Recruitment has begun locally, with practical training provided on site. Bramble Foods said the investment supports demand for smaller packs without requiring an extension to the bakery building. Total spending remains within the approved project budget.

Posted: Monday, October 5, 2026
Posted by: Elin Veymar

Oakhill Bakeries Group has confirmed the closure of its Ostara bakery following consultation with employees. The decision affects 31 roles. The company considered proposals for shorter production weeks, a smaller product range and additional contract baking, but none provided enough regular work to cover the site's costs.

Nineteen employees have accepted roles elsewhere in the group: 11 at Amberford and eight at Kestrel Bay. Twelve employees remain at risk of redundancy and have received individual statements setting out their payments and support. Transfer offers include travel assistance for an initial six-month period.

The Ostara bakery remains in production while customer orders are transferred in stages. Staff have paid time for interviews and employment advice. Managing director Tessa Oakhill thanked employees for their proposals and said the decision reflects the building's operating costs and low utilisation, rather than the quality of their work.

News release

Amberford electricity connection delays prompt formal improvement notice

Published: 6 October 2026

The Kestria Energy Board has issued a formal improvement notice to the Amberford electricity network operator after an audit found repeated delays in providing connection quotations. Of 160 complete applications examined, 47 had not received a quotation within the required 15 working days.

The applications covered small shops, workshops and housing developments. The longest recorded wait was 38 working days. The operator attributed the backlog to vacancies and incomplete internal handovers. The Board found that these problems did not remove its obligation to meet the published service standard.

The notice requires weekly reporting of outstanding quotations and a named contact for every affected applicant. It also requires the operator to separate applications awaiting customer information from those delayed within its own teams. The notice imposes no financial penalty. Applicants can ask the operator for a written explanation of their case and use the Board's complaints route if it remains unresolved.

Ostara industrial gas restrictions lifted after equipment repairs

Supply restrictions on the East Ostara industrial gas branch have been lifted following repairs to a pressure regulator. The Kestria Energy Board confirmed the change after reviewing test records supplied by the network operator. The branch has returned to its normal available capacity of 92 megawatt hours per hour.

The restrictions affected 14 sites with interruptible supply agreements from 22 September. The operator recorded a total requested reduction of 16 megawatt hours per hour during the restriction period. It has reported no interruption to household supplies and no loss of gas containment associated with the equipment fault.

Affected businesses have received individual notices cancelling their temporary limits. The Board has requested maintenance records and an explanation of how the fault developed. September figures show shorter queues at freight gates

Mara Venn 5 Oct 2026

Average lorry turnaround time at the Port of Kestrel Bay fell to 39 minutes in September, compared with 43 minutes in July. The monthly figure covers 31,480 completed visits and includes time spent waiting inside the terminal. Visits cancelled before arrival are excluded.

The port handled 82,900 standard container units during September. This was 2.4 per cent above the same month last year, despite the wind stoppage on 3 September and the reduced working length at Berth Four. Rail accounted for 29 per cent of containers leaving the port by land.

Gate staff recorded fewer arrivals without bookings after hauliers began receiving an additional booking reminder in August. Unbooked arrivals fell from 412 in August to 267 in September. The authority asks drivers to check the container release status before travelling, as a gate booking alone does not confirm that cargo is ready for collection.

Port publishes revised charges for empty container storage

Tomas Bellwick 29 Sep 2026

The Port of Kestrel Bay published a revised empty-container storage tariff today. Under the tariff now in force, the first five calendar days remain free. Storage from day six to day ten costs KRN 18 per standard container unit per day, compared with KRN 15 under the previous tariff.

The rate from day eleven is KRN 31 per unit per day, an increase of KRN 4. Loaded-container storage, vessel dues and rail handling charges are unchanged. Containers already in the empty yard before today remain subject to the previous rates for their current stay.

Empty containers occupied an average of 81 per cent of designated yard spaces during August. The revised charges follow a tariff review circulated to account holders in July. Customers can view the applicable rate and arrival date for each container in their account record, or request a written breakdown from the port billing team.

Maintenance vacancies remain hardest to fill in autumn survey

Media centre · Tomas Bellan
9 October

Maintenance roles remain the hardest vacancies for food manufacturers to fill, according to a staffing survey released today by the Food Manufacturers Federation of Kestria. Seventy-six member businesses responded between 22 September and 2 October.

Among the 49 respondents recruiting during that period, 29 reported difficulty hiring maintenance staff. Twenty-one reported difficulty recruiting machine operators. Businesses could select more than one role, so the figures do not represent separate groups of employers.

Tomas Bellan, research manager, said: “Employers described a shortage of applicants with experience of fault finding and routine equipment care. Several businesses in Kestrel Bay said vacancies had increased their reliance on external repair services.”

Thirty-two respondents said they had increased internal training during the previous six months. The federation is using the findings in discussions with training providers in Amberford and Ostara. The survey did not measure the effect of the proposed wage settlement announced this week.

Manufacturers seek simpler rules for proposed packaging levy

Media centre · Mara Vennick
28 August

The Food Manufacturers Federation of Kestria has called for changes to a proposed packaging levy, saying the current draft would require manufacturers to report the same material more than once.

In its submission to the Ministry of Revenue, the federation supports charging by packaging weight but asks for a single reporting return. The proposal sets a rate of KRN 0.18 per kilogram for certain packaging materials.

A review of records from 26 member businesses found that 19 would need to change their stock systems under the draft rules. Smaller manufacturers estimated an average initial cost of KRN 8,400, excluding staff time.

Mara Vennick, the federation’s policy director, said: “Members need clear definitions and a practical way to submit figures. One return, with worked examples, would help businesses meet the rules and make the information easier to check.”

Trading in wheat, oat and rapeseed futures resumed at 10:05 today after an interruption to the exchange's order entry service. Ostara Commodities Exchange suspended matching at 09:12 when monitoring identified delays in order acknowledgements. A ten-minute period for members to review and cancel orders preceded the reopening.

Trades completed before the suspension remain valid. Orders that had been accepted and remained unfilled were retained with their original priority. Kestrel Bay trustees directed to replace incomplete pension records

Written by Leila Corven

The Pensions Oversight Authority has directed the trustees of the Merehaven Packaging Retirement Plan in Kestrel Bay to repair incomplete membership records. An inspection found missing service dates or pay histories for 417 of the plan's 2,860 members. These records are needed to calculate promised retirement benefits accurately.

The trustees must produce a costed repair programme within 30 days and complete the work by 31 March 2027. They must also arrange an independent check of corrected records and send monthly progress reports to the Authority. The direction follows an earlier request for improvements that was not completed.

The inspection did not find evidence that assets were missing. Existing pension payments will continue, and the administrator will contact members if it needs information from them. Members should retain old benefit statements and employment records where available. The trustees have 28 days to appeal against the direction.

Trustees asked to check member addresses before annual statements

Written by Celia Bramwell

The Pensions Oversight Authority is asking workplace pension trustees to check their member contact records before issuing annual benefit statements this autumn. A review of 120 plans found that 8.4 per cent of statements sent during the previous reporting cycle were returned or could not be delivered electronically.

Plans should compare their records with recent updates from members and employers, investigate returned post and provide a straightforward way to correct an address. Trustees should take particular care with former employees who still hold benefits in the plan. An employer's current payroll list will not necessarily include these members.

The Authority has published a short checklist covering address checks, secure identity verification and records of delivery failures. Members who have moved should contact their pension administrator using details from an existing statement. They should never be asked to pay a fee simply to update their postal or email address.

Les délais de traitement diminuent pour le crédit régional

Par Lucien Dorselin

Publié le 8 octobre 2026

Le délai médian de traitement des dossiers complets du crédit régional à l’investissement productif s’établit à 19 jours ouvrables en septembre, comparativement à 27 en août. L’Agence de développement économique de Val-Brume publie aujourd’hui cet indicateur avec le nombre de décisions rendues. Il mesure la période entre la réception d’un dossier complet et la transmission de la décision.

En septembre, l’Agence a rendu 38 décisions : 33 attestations favorables et cinq refus. Les dépenses reconnues dans les dossiers acceptés totalisent 8,4 millions de KRN, pour des crédits de 1 008 000 KRN. Les refus concernent des équipements non admissibles ou des dépenses engagées hors de la période couverte par le programme.

Le formulaire simplifié, offert depuis le 1er septembre, facilite la vérification des montants déclarés. Une réaffectation interne a aussi ajouté une personne à l’équipe d’analyse. Le délai publié n’est pas une garantie individuelle : les dossiers qui nécessitent des précisions peuvent demander davantage de temps. L’attestation de l’Agence ne constitue pas un versement de fonds.

Un soutien de proximité pour les commerces de Clairvallon

Par Maëlle Vardelin

Publié le 10 septembre 2026

Neuf commerces de Clairvallon bénéficient d’un soutien total de 342 000 KRN pour adapter leurs locaux et améliorer leur fonctionnement. L’Agence de développement économique de Val-Brume a confirmé ces aides dans le cadre du programme Commerce de proximité. Les investissements admissibles des entreprises totalisent 855 000 KRN.

Les projets comprennent l’installation de portes accessibles, le remplacement de chambres froides et l’aménagement de zones de préparation de commandes. L’Épicerie des Aulnes reçoit notamment 48 000 KRN pour réorganiser sa réserve et remplacer deux appareils de réfrigération. La Maison du Fil de Brume obtient 21 000 KRN pour adapter son entrée et son espace de service.

Chaque contribution représente 40 % des dépenses reconnues. Les travaux de décoration et les achats destinés à la revente sont exclus. Les commerces retenus comptent ensemble 61 emplois, mais les conventions ne présentent pas ce nombre comme une création d’emplois. Le suivi porte sur les factures, la réalisation des aménagements approuvés et le maintien de l’activité dans les locaux concernés.

Press release

Financial stability review highlights commercial property refinancing risks

Published on 5 October 2026

Kestria's banking system has sufficient capital to absorb substantial losses, but commercial property lending warrants close attention, according to the Bank of Kestria's financial stability review published today. Regulated banks reported an aggregate core capital ratio of 15.6 per cent at the end of June, compared with 15.2 per cent a year earlier.

The review estimates that KRN 8.7 billion of commercial property loans require refinancing within twelve months. Office buildings in Saltmarsh and warehouse developments around Kestrel Bay account for a large share. Lower rental income could make refinancing harder even following September's reduction in the policy rate.

In the Bank's adverse scenario, property values fall by 25 per cent and unemployment rises sharply. Aggregate bank capital remains above minimum requirements, although outcomes vary between lenders. The scenario is a resilience test, not a forecast. The Bank has asked lenders to strengthen records on lease expiry dates and borrower cash flows.

Notes for editors

Press release

Settlement system completes recovery exercise from Amberford backup site

Published on 28 September 2026

The Bank of Kestria has completed a recovery exercise for the system that settles large payments between regulated banks. During the exercise on 27 September, staff transferred test operations from Saltmarsh to the Bank's backup site in Amberford. The exercise used simulated payment instructions and did not move customer funds.

All 14 participating institutions connected successfully to the backup service. Processing resumed after 43 minutes, within the Bank's internal recovery limit of 60 minutes. The test included the loss of a primary communications link and a check that completed instructions could not be processed twice.

Observers identified two areas for improvement: clearer contact arrangements during staff changes and faster confirmation that every participant had received the recovery message. Neither affected the completion of the exercise. The Bank has assigned corrective actions and will track them through its operational risk programme. Normal settlement services remained available throughout.

Notes for editors

August goods imports rise faster than export values

By Nessa Talvern, Head of Trade Statistics

9 October 2026, 12:00

Kestria's goods trade deficit widened to KRN 710 million in August, from KRN 540 million in July. Exports totalled KRN 4.86 billion and imports totalled KRN 5.57 billion. Seasonally adjusted export values increased by 0.8 per cent over the month, while import values increased by 3.9 per cent.

Higher machinery and fuel imports contributed most to the wider deficit. Export growth was concentrated in processed food, while electrical equipment exports declined slightly after July's increase. Businesses in the Ostara industrial area reported several large machinery deliveries, illustrating how individual purchases can affect monthly trade totals.

Over the three months to August, exports were 1.7 per cent higher than in the previous three months and imports were 2.2 per cent higher. These comparisons use values at current prices. They therefore reflect changes in prices as well as quantities. July totals are unchanged from the previous release.

Employment grows as July unemployment rate holds steady

By Tovan Merrow, Head of Labour Market Statistics

26 August 2026, 12:15

Kestria had an estimated 2,846,000 people in employment in July, an increase of 7,000 from June. The seasonally adjusted unemployment rate remained at 5.4 per cent. An estimated 162,000 people were unemployed, meaning they were without work, available to start and actively seeking a job.

Employment increased most in accommodation, food services and building maintenance. Manufacturing employment changed little. The employment rate for people aged 16 to 64 rose to 73.1 per cent from 73.0 per cent. These estimates come from the household labour survey and cover employees and people working for themselves.

Survey responses from Kestrel Bay indicated stronger seasonal hiring, although local monthly estimates are less reliable than the national figures. The Kestria Statistics Office advises users to consider several months together. Small monthly movements may reflect sampling variation rather than a lasting change in the labour market.

Revenue Service reports progress on sales tax refunds

Date: 08/10/2026

The Kestria Revenue Service processed 92 per cent of complete sales tax refund claims within 15 working days during September. This compares with 86 per cent in August. September payments totalled KRN 18.4 million across 1,760 claims, including claims from manufacturers, wholesalers and building contractors.

The improvement followed the reassignment of six processing staff to the refund team in Ostara. Claims requiring further checks are excluded from the 15-day measure while the service waits for requested information. The published figures include both the number of claims awaiting checks and the reasons for those checks.

At the end of September, 214 claims were awaiting invoices, bank account confirmation or an explanation of unusually large purchases. Businesses can check progress through their tax account. Sending the same claim again can delay processing because staff must establish whether it is a duplicate. A business should instead reply to the information request using its existing claim reference.

Payroll filing service restored after morning access problems

Date: 10/09/2026

Access to the Kestria Revenue Service payroll filing service was restored at 11.40 am today following a technical fault. The interruption began at 8.15 am and affected employers trying to open or submit payroll tax returns. Corporate tax and sales tax filing remained available.

The fault interrupted the connection between the sign-in page and payroll records. Technical checks found no evidence that employer or employee information had been lost or disclosed. Returns submitted before the interruption remain recorded, and employers do not need to send those returns again.

Employers who saw an error message during submission should check their filing history for a receipt number. If no receipt appears, they should reopen the saved return and submit it. The service logged 186 reports from employers, including businesses in Amberford and Kestrel Bay. Anyone still unable to file should contact the payroll support team and quote the message shown on screen.

Workshop report identifies recurring questions from accounts preparers

Last modified 7 October 2026 · 2 minute read

The Accounting Standards Council of Kestria has published a report on its four autumn workshops. A total of 163 people attended sessions in Saltmarsh, Kestrel Bay, Ostara and Val-Brume between 10 September and 1 October.

Questions informing future support

Participants submitted 58 questions before the sessions and raised further examples during discussion. Staff grouped the questions by topic, with revenue recognition and repair provisions accounting for just over half of the advance submissions.

  • Evidence supporting repair estimates
  • Revenue from partly completed deliveries
  • Choosing useful accounting policy information
  • Explaining changes in estimates

The report summarises recurring difficulties and includes six examples drawn from the sessions, with company details replaced by invented facts. It explains the standards in force during the workshops. The revenue amendments issued on 6 October are available separately. Staff will use the findings when proposing next year's educational programme; the report itself introduces no accounting requirements.

Council seeks views on clearer supplier finance disclosures

Last modified 19 August 2026 · 2 minute read

The Accounting Standards Council of Kestria has published proposed amendments to Kestrian Accounting Standard 14, Cash Flows and Financing. The proposals would require companies to explain arrangements under which a finance provider pays suppliers and the company later pays that provider.

Information proposed

The draft would introduce a single note showing the size and main terms of these arrangements. Companies would retain responsibility for deciding how the related liabilities and cash flows are classified under existing requirements.

  • Opening and closing liability balances
  • Amounts already paid to suppliers
  • Ranges of payment due dates
  • Significant changes without cash movements

Comments are invited by 30 September 2026. The Council particularly welcomes examples from manufacturers and wholesalers in Amberford and Ostara. Its initial proposal is for annual periods beginning on or after 1 January 2028, with early application permitted. The final requirements and transition arrangements will depend on the evidence received.

Kestrian Food Producers Maintain Stable Outlook as Input Costs Ease

9 October 2026 | Written by Céline Arvane

Meridian Ratings has maintained a stable outlook for Kestria’s packaged food sector. Lower grain and container costs are helping producers rebuild margins, although household spending remains subdued. Across six rated companies, average operating margins increased to 11.2% in the first half of 2026 from 10.4% a year earlier.

Sales volumes rose just 0.8%, with stronger demand for basic products offset by weaker purchases of premium lines. Producers supplying retailers in Saltmarsh and Amberford reported increased use of promotions. Meridian expects price competition to limit how much of the recent cost relief companies retain.

The sector’s median net debt stood at 2.4 times operating profit before depreciation at June. Most rated producers have sufficient cash and committed facilities for planned investment over the next year. Debt-funded acquisitions or prolonged discounting would create greater pressure than the modest volume growth currently assumed in Meridian’s forecasts.

Meridian Rates Saltmarsh Waterworks Bond in Line With Issuer Rating

10 September 2026 | Written by Mara Ternell

Meridian Ratings has assigned an A minus rating to Saltmarsh Waterworks’ proposed KRN 180 million senior unsecured bond. The issue rating matches the company’s long-term issuer rating, which remains A minus with a stable outlook. The bond is expected to mature in September 2033.

The company intends to use KRN 120 million of the proceeds to repay a bank loan due in February 2027. The balance will fund pipe replacement and treatment equipment within its existing investment programme. The transaction would extend debt maturities while leaving total borrowing within Meridian’s previous forecasts.

The proposed bonds will rank equally with the company’s other senior unsecured obligations. Meridian’s assessment assumes that the final terms are consistent with the draft documents reviewed. Cost overruns or a material increase in borrowing beyond the current programme could weaken financial headroom, but neither is included in the base forecast.

Ostara workshop will explain bond disclosure duties to smaller issuers

Published
6 October 2026
Author
Lucien Marcelet
Reference
KSC-2026-836

The Kestria Securities Commission will hold a free workshop in Ostara on 22 October for smaller companies that issue bonds to the public. The session will explain continuing disclosure duties, including how to report borrowing conditions, missed payments and material changes in available funding.

There are 60 places available, with registration closing on 19 October unless the session fills earlier. Finance staff, company secretaries and directors may attend. Commission staff will use fictional examples involving a KRN 15 million bond issue and a loan approaching its repayment date. Attendance does not satisfy any formal reporting requirement.

Participants may submit general questions when registering. Staff cannot give advance approval to company announcements or discuss confidential supervisory cases at the workshop. Written materials will be available in English and French, and a French-language online session will be arranged separately. The Commission will publish the presentation materials so that issuers unable to attend can use the same guidance.

Commission publishes findings from review of market announcement timing

Published
7 September 2026
Author
Selin Arvane
Reference
KSC-2026-808

The Kestria Securities Commission has completed a review of how quickly listed companies publish information that could affect their securities prices. Staff examined 63 announcements issued between January and June, including notices about cancelled contracts, financing agreements and significant changes to expected earnings.

In 11 cases, companies could not provide a clear record of when senior staff first received the information. Five companies relied on a single person to approve announcements, with no cover during absences. The Commission has written to those companies requesting improvements to their procedures.

The findings do not establish that all 11 companies disclosed information late. However, incomplete records make it harder to demonstrate compliance. Companies should record key decisions, identify an alternative approver and keep disclosure arrangements under review. A briefing note published today includes practical examples. The Commission will assess the responses before deciding whether any individual case requires further investigation.

Bracken Grid Bond Rating Holds After Amberford Storm Disruption

By Tomas Arven and Mara Vellin
October 9, 2026

Northstar Credit Analytics has maintained Bracken Grid's BBB senior unsecured bond rating and stable outlook following the 6 October storm in the Amberford district. The storm damaged overhead lines and interrupted supplies to 74,000 connections. By the evening of 8 October, the company had restored power to all but 1,900 affected connections.

Bracken Grid's preliminary estimate places repair costs at KRN 18 million to KRN 24 million. Northstar has assumed the full upper estimate in its initial assessment without relying on insurance receipts. The company had KRN 72 million in cash and KRN 110 million of undrawn committed facilities at the end of September.

These resources should allow repairs to proceed without materially weakening liquidity. The rating also allows for occasional weather-related disruption. Northstar will review the final repair bill, compensation payments and any changes to planned maintenance. Costs substantially above the current estimate, or evidence of wider network weaknesses, could alter the assessment.

Ostara Rental Housing Outlook Remains Stable Despite Higher Maintenance Spending

By Mara Vellin and Dario Selven
October 8, 2026

Northstar Credit Analytics has maintained a stable sector outlook for rated rental housing companies operating in Ostara. High occupancy and steady rent collection continue to support earnings, although repairs and borrowing costs are absorbing more cash. The assessment covers four issuers with a combined 28,400 homes.

Average occupancy stood at 97.4% at the end of August, compared with 97.1% a year earlier. Rent arrears remained modest at 1.8% of annual billed rent. Maintenance spending rose 8%, led by roof repairs and heating replacements. Fixed interest rates apply to 76% of the sample's debt, limiting the immediate effect of higher financing costs.

Northstar expects most issuers to fund routine repairs from rental income while keeping development programmes within committed borrowing limits. Ratings could come under pressure where large construction projects coincide with debt maturities. The stable sector outlook assumes occupancy remains above 96% and companies retain enough accessible funding to meet twelve months of planned spending.

Ostara businesses offered working capital review appointments this month

Tomas Arlen · 6 October 2026

Harrow & Finch Bank is offering 30 working capital review appointments for mid-sized businesses at its Ostara branch between 12 and 30 October. The sessions are intended for companies preparing for seasonal changes in stock purchases, customer payments or supplier bills.

Each appointment lasts up to an hour and carries no charge. Businesses should bring a thirteen-week cash-flow forecast, a list of unpaid customer invoices and details of existing borrowing. A relationship manager will discuss the timing of expected receipts and payments and identify any information needed for a lending application.

Attendance does not require a company to move its banking arrangements. Any subsequent request for an overdraft or loan will be assessed separately, with rates and fees explained before acceptance. Telephone appointments are available for businesses outside Ostara that cannot attend the branch during the scheduled period.

Bank publishes revised fees for business lending administration

Leonie Venn · 2 September 2026

Harrow & Finch Bank has published a revised schedule of business lending administration fees, taking effect on 5 October. The fee for a borrower-requested security amendment will fall from KRN 450 to KRN 325. Providing a duplicate annual interest certificate will become free, replacing the current KRN 35 charge.

The fee for reviewing a request to extend an overdraft temporarily will rise from KRN 175 to KRN 225. It covers the review and does not guarantee approval. Customers will be told whether a charge applies before they ask the bank to proceed with any chargeable work.

The changes do not alter agreed loan margins or repayment dates. Where an existing agreement fixes an administration fee, that agreement will continue to apply. The full schedule is available from relationship teams and on the bank’s website, with copies in French available for customers in Val-Brume.

Ostara depot changes cut damaged produce deliveries by nearly a quarter

8 October 2026Idris Weller, Corporate Affairs

GreenBasket Supermarkets has reduced damaged fruit and vegetable deliveries from its Ostara depot by 24 per cent following changes to packing and loading. The result compares damage recorded per thousand crates during July to September with the same three months of 2025.

The depot supplies 68 stores and handles about 410,000 produce crates each month. Changes included shallower crates for soft fruit, separate loading positions for heavier root vegetables and temperature checks at each loading bay. GreenBasket spent KRN 1.7 million on equipment and training for the work.

Depot manager Brenna Holt said staff had recorded where damage occurred before changing handling routines. The measured reduction represents approximately 7,800 fewer damaged crates over the quarter. Produce rejected by stores remains subject to the same quality checks, and items suitable for sale are assessed separately from stock that must be discarded.

GreenBasket recalls selected oat biscuits after incorrect allergen labelling

9 September 2026Sofia Merrow, Corporate Affairs

GreenBasket Supermarkets is recalling its 250-gram Honeyfield Oat Biscuits with batch code HB0902 and a best-before date of 18 February 2027. The affected packs contain milk, which is missing from the allergen statement. They are unsuitable for people with a milk allergy.

The biscuits were sold in 87 GreenBasket stores across Kestria between 3 and 8 September. Customers with a milk allergy should not eat them. Anyone who bought an affected pack can return it to any GreenBasket store for a full refund without a receipt. Other batch codes are not included in this recall.

GreenBasket identified the error during a packaging check yesterday and removed the affected stock from sale that evening. Recall notices are displayed in the relevant stores and on the customer website. Product safety manager Orla Venn said the company had received no reports of illness linked to the affected batch.

Val-Brume stores introduce clearer French labels across household essentials

6 Oct 2026

Lumen Home Retail has introduced clearer French-language shelf labels at its three Val-Brume stores. The change covers 2,300 household and grocery products, including cleaning supplies, bedding and cupboard staples. Product names, pack sizes and unit prices now appear together in a larger, consistent format.

The work follows an eight-week review with customers and store colleagues in Kestria's French-speaking region. Participants said that unit prices were sometimes difficult to locate and that several household product descriptions needed simpler wording. Printed guidance at service desks and online collection instructions have also been revised.

The project cost KRN 210,000, including translation, printing and staff training. It does not change product prices or the ranges stocked. Lumen will collect feedback at the three stores through November and check a sample of labels each week for accuracy. Customers can report unclear wording at any service desk or through the retailer's website.

New Ostara bakery agreement brings daily deliveries to more stores

16 Sep 2026

Lumen Home Retail has signed a three-year supply agreement with Hearthmere Baking, a family-owned producer based in Ostara. From 21 September, the bakery will supply bread and rolls to 14 Lumen stores, extending an existing arrangement covering six branches. The agreement is worth an estimated KRN 7.2 million over its term.

Hearthmere has installed an additional oven and created nine production and packing jobs to support the wider service. Deliveries will reach stores before opening on six mornings each week. The range includes a small sliced loaf developed after customers asked for more choices suited to smaller households.

Lumen will provide weekly order forecasts and pay agreed invoices within 21 days. Both businesses will review unsold quantities each month, with the aim of reducing surplus without leaving shelves empty late in the day. Existing bakery suppliers will continue serving Lumen stores outside the expanded delivery area.

Kestrel Bay Loading Repairs Restore Normal Grain Dispatch Capacity

OSTARA, Kestria, Oct. 6, 2026 /KestriaWire/ -- Prairie Gold Grain Co-operative has restored normal dispatch capacity at its Kestrel Bay store after replacing a worn bearing in the grain loading conveyor. The conveyor returned to service on 5 October following an inspection and an unloaded test. Grain receiving continued while the equipment was unavailable.

The interruption delayed nine customer collections carrying a combined 270 tonnes of wheat and oats. Six have now been completed, and revised collection times have been agreed for the remaining three. No grain was damaged, and the affected conveyor did not require any stored stock to be discarded.

The loading line is again operating at its normal rate of up to 90 tonnes an hour, subject to vehicle changes and sampling. Customers should use the collection time shown on their latest dispatch confirmation. Drivers arriving early must wait in the marked parking area until called to the loading point.

About Prairie Gold Grain Co-operative
Prairie Gold is owned by 4,100 farming families and handles about a fifth of Kestria's wheat and oat harvest.

Early Wheat Samples Show Firm Protein And Low Moisture

OSTARA, Kestria, Sept. 7, 2026 /KestriaWire/ -- The first new-season quality report from Prairie Gold Grain Co-operative shows average wheat protein of 12.6 per cent and average moisture of 13.2 per cent. The report covers 186 accepted loads, representing 5,920 tonnes delivered to the Amberford and Ostara receiving sites by 6 September.

Average wheat test weight was 78.4 kilogrammes per hectolitre. These results support the sale of several parcels for milling, although each customer contract has its own requirements. The samples mainly represent earlier-harvested fields and should not be treated as a measure of the whole crop.

Oat deliveries remain limited, with 740 tonnes accepted so far. Members can request the test results for their own loads through the receiving office. Any request for a second test must identify the delivery ticket, allowing staff to locate the sealed sample retained from that load.

Corvel publishes evidence sheets for selected carton recycling claims

By Tobin Merrow · October 9, 2026
Share: LinkedIn X Email

Corvel Packaging has issued evidence sheets for 18 uncoated carton specifications supplied from Amberford. Each sheet identifies the board grade, coatings, inks and adhesives covered by the assessment. It also explains the conditions attached to the company's recycling statements.

The sheets draw on fibre separation tests and checks of collection guidance available in Saltmarsh, Amberford and Val-Brume. Results apply only to the listed specifications. Cartons with film windows, barrier layers or heavy food contamination require separate consideration and are outside the scope of this release.

Customers can request a sheet using their carton specification number. The documents support packaging decisions but do not establish that every local collection service accepts a carton. Corvel advises customers to check disposal wording against the collection arrangements serving their buyers. No new recycling claim has been added to customer artwork as part of this work.

Across eight weeks of measured production, trim represented 13.1 per cent of material fed into the lines, down from 16.4 per cent during the preceding eight weeks.

The comparison covers the same four tray designs and excludes trial runs. Staff adjusted the spacing between tray shapes and replaced worn cutting edges. The plant used 18 tonnes less sheet material than it would have used at the earlier trim rate for the recorded volume.

Tray dimensions, sealing surfaces and approved material specifications are unchanged. Clean trim from these lines is separated for controlled reprocessing, subject to the requirements of each product specification. Corvel is reporting the reduction as a material efficiency measure; it has not calculated a carbon saving from the work.

Amberford bakery prepares new packing line for autumn commissioning

By Leonie Varnet

28 August 2026

Bramble Foods has completed the main installation work on a new packing line at its Amberford bakery. The KRN 8.4 million project replaces two older machines used for small cake packs and is scheduled to enter commissioning in October. Electrical checks and staff training will take place during September.

Once fully operational, the line is expected to increase the site's cake packing capacity by 18% and reduce film waste per pack by about 11%. These estimates will be checked during production trials. The bakery will continue supplying customers through its existing equipment while the new line is tested.

The project includes 14 additional permanent roles across production, maintenance and quality control. Recruitment has begun locally, with practical training provided on site. Bramble Foods said the investment supports demand for smaller packs without requiring an extension to the bakery building. Total spending remains within the approved project budget.

Posted: Monday, October 5, 2026
Posted by: Elin Veymar

Oakhill Bakeries Group has confirmed the closure of its Ostara bakery following consultation with employees. The decision affects 31 roles. The company considered proposals for shorter production weeks, a smaller product range and additional contract baking, but none provided enough regular work to cover the site's costs.

Nineteen employees have accepted roles elsewhere in the group: 11 at Amberford and eight at Kestrel Bay. Twelve employees remain at risk of redundancy and have received individual statements setting out their payments and support. Transfer offers include travel assistance for an initial six-month period.

The Ostara bakery remains in production while customer orders are transferred in stages. Staff have paid time for interviews and employment advice. Managing director Tessa Oakhill thanked employees for their proposals and said the decision reflects the building's operating costs and low utilisation, rather than the quality of their work.

News release

Amberford electricity connection delays prompt formal improvement notice

Published: 6 October 2026

The Kestria Energy Board has issued a formal improvement notice to the Amberford electricity network operator after an audit found repeated delays in providing connection quotations. Of 160 complete applications examined, 47 had not received a quotation within the required 15 working days.

The applications covered small shops, workshops and housing developments. The longest recorded wait was 38 working days. The operator attributed the backlog to vacancies and incomplete internal handovers. The Board found that these problems did not remove its obligation to meet the published service standard.

The notice requires weekly reporting of outstanding quotations and a named contact for every affected applicant. It also requires the operator to separate applications awaiting customer information from those delayed within its own teams. The notice imposes no financial penalty. Applicants can ask the operator for a written explanation of their case and use the Board's complaints route if it remains unresolved.

Ostara industrial gas restrictions lifted after equipment repairs

Published: 29 September 2026

Supply restrictions on the East Ostara industrial gas branch have been lifted following repairs to a pressure regulator. The Kestria Energy Board confirmed the change after reviewing test records supplied by the network operator. The branch has returned to its normal available capacity of 92 megawatt hours per hour.

It has reported no interruption to household supplies and no loss of gas containment associated with the equipment fault.

Affected businesses have received individual notices cancelling their temporary limits. The Board has requested maintenance records and an explanation of how the fault developed. September figures show shorter queues at freight gates

Mara Venn 5 Oct 2026

Average lorry turnaround time at the Port of Kestrel Bay fell to 39 minutes in September, compared with 43 minutes in July. The monthly figure covers 31,480 completed visits and includes time spent waiting inside the terminal. Visits cancelled before arrival are excluded.

The port handled 82,900 standard container units during September. This was 2.4 per cent above the same month last year, despite the wind stoppage on 3 September and the reduced working length at Berth Four. Rail accounted for 29 per cent of containers leaving the port by land.

Gate staff recorded fewer arrivals without bookings after hauliers began receiving an additional booking reminder in August. Unbooked arrivals fell from 412 in August to 267 in September. The authority asks drivers to check the container release status before travelling, as a gate booking alone does not confirm that cargo is ready for collection.

Port publishes revised charges for empty container storage

Tomas Bellwick 29 Sep 2026

The Port of Kestrel Bay published a revised empty-container storage tariff today. Under the tariff now in force, the first five calendar days remain free. Storage from day six to day ten costs KRN 18 per standard container unit per day, compared with KRN 15 under the previous tariff.

The rate from day eleven is KRN 31 per unit per day, an increase of KRN 4. Loaded-container storage, vessel dues and rail handling charges are unchanged. Containers already in the empty yard before today remain subject to the previous rates for their current stay.

Empty containers occupied an average of 81 per cent of designated yard spaces during August. The revised charges follow a tariff review circulated to account holders in July. Customers can view the applicable rate and arrival date for each container in their account record, or request a written breakdown from the port billing team.

Maintenance vacancies remain hardest to fill in autumn survey

Media centre · Tomas Bellan
9 October

Maintenance roles remain the hardest vacancies for food manufacturers to fill, according to a staffing survey released today by the Food Manufacturers Federation of Kestria. Seventy-six member businesses responded between 22 September and 2 October.

Among the 49 respondents recruiting during that period, 29 reported difficulty hiring maintenance staff. Twenty-one reported difficulty recruiting machine operators. Businesses could select more than one role, so the figures do not represent separate groups of employers.

Tomas Bellan, research manager, said: “Employers described a shortage of applicants with experience of fault finding and routine equipment care. Several businesses in Kestrel Bay said vacancies had increased their reliance on external repair services.”

Thirty-two respondents said they had increased internal training during the previous six months. The federation is using the findings in discussions with training providers in Amberford and Ostara. The survey did not measure the effect of the proposed wage settlement announced this week.

Manufacturers seek simpler rules for proposed packaging levy

Media centre · Mara Vennick
28 August

The Food Manufacturers Federation of Kestria has called for changes to a proposed packaging levy, saying the current draft would require manufacturers to report the same material more than once.

In its submission to the Ministry of Revenue, the federation supports charging by packaging weight but asks for a single reporting return. The proposal sets a rate of KRN 0.18 per kilogram for certain packaging materials.

A review of records from 26 member businesses found that 19 would need to change their stock systems under the draft rules. Smaller manufacturers estimated an average initial cost of KRN 8,400, excluding staff time.

Mara Vennick, the federation’s policy director, said: “Members need clear definitions and a practical way to submit figures. One return, with worked examples, would help businesses meet the rules and make the information easier to check.”

Kestrel Bay trustees directed to replace incomplete pension records

Written by Leila Corven

The Pensions Oversight Authority has directed the trustees of the Merehaven Packaging Retirement Plan in Kestrel Bay to repair incomplete membership records. An inspection found missing service dates or pay histories for 417 of the plan's 2,860 members. These records are needed to calculate promised retirement benefits accurately.

The trustees must produce a costed repair programme within 30 days and complete the work by 31 March 2027. They must also arrange an independent check of corrected records and send monthly progress reports to the Authority. The direction follows an earlier request for improvements that was not completed.

The inspection did not find evidence that assets were missing. Existing pension payments will continue, and the administrator will contact members if it needs information from them. Members should retain old benefit statements and employment records where available. The trustees have 28 days to appeal against the direction.

Trustees asked to check member addresses before annual statements

Written by Celia Bramwell

The Pensions Oversight Authority is asking workplace pension trustees to check their member contact records before issuing annual benefit statements this autumn. A review of 120 plans found that 8.4 per cent of statements sent during the previous reporting cycle were returned or could not be delivered electronically.

Plans should compare their records with recent updates from members and employers, investigate returned post and provide a straightforward way to correct an address. Trustees should take particular care with former employees who still hold benefits in the plan. An employer's current payroll list will not necessarily include these members.

The Authority has published a short checklist covering address checks, secure identity verification and records of delivery failures. Members who have moved should contact their pension administrator using details from an existing statement. They should never be asked to pay a fee simply to update their postal or email address.

Trading resumes after morning interruption to order entry

Notice No. 2026/362 · Category: Trading hours

Date of issue: 08.10.2026 · Effective: 15.10.2026

Trading in wheat, oat and rapeseed futures resumed at 10:05 today after an interruption to the exchange's order entry service. Ostara Commodities Exchange suspended matching at 09:12 when monitoring identified delays in order acknowledgements. A ten-minute period for members to review and cancel orders preceded the reopening.

Trades completed before the suspension remain valid. Orders that had been accepted and remained unfilled were retained with their original priority. Messages that did not receive an acceptance acknowledgement were not added to the order book. Members were asked to reconcile their records against the exchange's order and trade reports before entering replacement instructions.

Technical staff traced the interruption to a fault in a message queue and moved the service to reserve equipment. The regular 16:30 closing time remains in place. Clearing and warehouse reporting services continued to operate during the interruption. The exchange is reviewing system records and member reports to establish why the fault was not resolved automatically.

Wheat margin requirements rise after increased market volatility

Notice No. 2026/348 · Category: Margins

Date of issue: 05.10.2026 · Effective: 12.10.2026

Ostara Commodities Exchange has raised the initial margin for wheat futures from KRN 1,600 to KRN 1,900 per contract. The maintenance margin increases from KRN 1,300 to KRN 1,550. The new requirements apply to all listed wheat months at today's clearing calculation, including positions opened before the announcement.

The adjustment reflects larger daily price movements and a greater concentration of positions in the nearest delivery month. Over the past five sessions, the average wheat price range was KRN 17 per tonne. Each contract covers 20 tonnes. The exchange has made no change to wheat delivery specifications or permitted price increments.

Clearing members must provide any additional collateral by 09:00 on the next trading day. Members may apply higher requirements to their own clients under their account agreements. Oat and rapeseed margins are unchanged by this notice. The exchange continues to assess both price risk and the time needed to close positions when setting its collateral requirements.

Market Operations, Ostara Commodities Exchange

Les délais de traitement diminuent pour le crédit régional

Par Lucien Dorselin

Publié le 8 octobre 2026

Le délai médian de traitement des dossiers complets du crédit régional à l’investissement productif s’établit à 19 jours ouvrables en septembre, comparativement à 27 en août. L’Agence de développement économique de Val-Brume publie aujourd’hui cet indicateur avec le nombre de décisions rendues. Il mesure la période entre la réception d’un dossier complet et la transmission de la décision.

En septembre, l’Agence a rendu 38 décisions : 33 attestations favorables et cinq refus. Les dépenses reconnues dans les dossiers acceptés totalisent 8,4 millions de KRN, pour des crédits de 1 008 000 KRN. Les refus concernent des équipements non admissibles ou des dépenses engagées hors de la période couverte par le programme.

Le formulaire simplifié, offert depuis le 1er septembre, facilite la vérification des montants déclarés. Une réaffectation interne a aussi ajouté une personne à l’équipe d’analyse. Le délai publié n’est pas une garantie individuelle : les dossiers qui nécessitent des précisions peuvent demander davantage de temps. L’attestation de l’Agence ne constitue pas un versement de fonds.

L’Épicerie des Aulnes reçoit notamment 48 000 KRN pour réorganiser sa réserve et remplacer deux appareils de réfrigération. La Maison du Fil de Brume obtient 21 000 KRN pour adapter son entrée et son espace de service.

Les commerces retenus comptent ensemble 61 emplois, mais les conventions ne présentent pas ce nombre comme une création d’emplois. August goods imports rise faster than export values

By Nessa Talvern, Head of Trade Statistics

9 October 2026, 12:00

Kestria's goods trade deficit widened to KRN 710 million in August, from KRN 540 million in July. Exports totalled KRN 4.86 billion and imports totalled KRN 5.57 billion. Seasonally adjusted export values increased by 0.8 per cent over the month, while import values increased by 3.9 per cent.

Higher machinery and fuel imports contributed most to the wider deficit. Export growth was concentrated in processed food, while electrical equipment exports declined slightly after July's increase. Businesses in the Ostara industrial area reported several large machinery deliveries, illustrating how individual purchases can affect monthly trade totals.

Over the three months to August, exports were 1.7 per cent higher than in the previous three months and imports were 2.2 per cent higher. These comparisons use values at current prices. They therefore reflect changes in prices as well as quantities. July totals are unchanged from the previous release.

Employment grows as July unemployment rate holds steady

By Tovan Merrow, Head of Labour Market Statistics

26 August 2026, 12:15

Kestria had an estimated 2,846,000 people in employment in July, an increase of 7,000 from June. The seasonally adjusted unemployment rate remained at 5.4 per cent. An estimated 162,000 people were unemployed, meaning they were without work, available to start and actively seeking a job.

Employment increased most in accommodation, food services and building maintenance. Manufacturing employment changed little. The employment rate for people aged 16 to 64 rose to 73.1 per cent from 73.0 per cent. These estimates come from the household labour survey and cover employees and people working for themselves.

Survey responses from Kestrel Bay indicated stronger seasonal hiring, although local monthly estimates are less reliable than the national figures. The Kestria Statistics Office advises users to consider several months together. Small monthly movements may reflect sampling variation rather than a lasting change in the labour market.

Press release

Financial stability review highlights commercial property refinancing risks

Published on 5 October 2026

Kestria's banking system has sufficient capital to absorb substantial losses, but commercial property lending warrants close attention, according to the Bank of Kestria's financial stability review published today. Regulated banks reported an aggregate core capital ratio of 15.6 per cent at the end of June, compared with 15.2 per cent a year earlier.

The review estimates that KRN 8.7 billion of commercial property loans require refinancing within twelve months. Office buildings in Saltmarsh and warehouse developments around Kestrel Bay account for a large share. Lower rental income could make refinancing harder even following September's reduction in the policy rate.

In the Bank's adverse scenario, property values fall by 25 per cent and unemployment rises sharply. Aggregate bank capital remains above minimum requirements, although outcomes vary between lenders. The scenario is a resilience test, not a forecast. The Bank has asked lenders to strengthen records on lease expiry dates and borrower cash flows.

Notes for editors

Press release

Settlement system completes recovery exercise from Amberford backup site

Published on 28 September 2026

The Bank of Kestria has completed a recovery exercise for the system that settles large payments between regulated banks. During the exercise on 27 September, staff transferred test operations from Saltmarsh to the Bank's backup site in Amberford. The exercise used simulated payment instructions and did not move customer funds.

All 14 participating institutions connected successfully to the backup service. Processing resumed after 43 minutes, within the Bank's internal recovery limit of 60 minutes. The test included the loss of a primary communications link and a check that completed instructions could not be processed twice.

Observers identified two areas for improvement: clearer contact arrangements during staff changes and faster confirmation that every participant had received the recovery message. Neither affected the completion of the exercise. The Bank has assigned corrective actions and will track them through its operational risk programme. Normal settlement services remained available throughout.

Notes for editors

Workshop report identifies recurring questions from accounts preparers

Last modified 7 October 2026 · 2 minute read

The Accounting Standards Council of Kestria has published a report on its four autumn workshops. A total of 163 people attended sessions in Saltmarsh, Kestrel Bay, Ostara and Val-Brume between 10 September and 1 October.

Questions informing future support

Participants submitted 58 questions before the sessions and raised further examples during discussion. Staff grouped the questions by topic, with revenue recognition and repair provisions accounting for just over half of the advance submissions.

  • Evidence supporting repair estimates
  • Revenue from partly completed deliveries
  • Choosing useful accounting policy information
  • Explaining changes in estimates

The report summarises recurring difficulties and includes six examples drawn from the sessions, with company details replaced by invented facts. It explains the standards in force during the workshops. The revenue amendments issued on 6 October are available separately. Staff will use the findings when proposing next year's educational programme; the report itself introduces no accounting requirements.

Council seeks views on clearer supplier finance disclosures

Last modified 19 August 2026 · 2 minute read

The Accounting Standards Council of Kestria has published proposed amendments to Kestrian Accounting Standard 14, Cash Flows and Financing. The proposals would require companies to explain arrangements under which a finance provider pays suppliers and the company later pays that provider.

Information proposed

The draft would introduce a single note showing the size and main terms of these arrangements. Companies would retain responsibility for deciding how the related liabilities and cash flows are classified under existing requirements.

  • Opening and closing liability balances
  • Amounts already paid to suppliers
  • Ranges of payment due dates
  • Significant changes without cash movements

Comments are invited by 30 September 2026. The Council particularly welcomes examples from manufacturers and wholesalers in Amberford and Ostara. Its initial proposal is for annual periods beginning on or after 1 January 2028, with early application permitted. The final requirements and transition arrangements will depend on the evidence received.

Revenue Service reports progress on sales tax refunds

Date: 08/10/2026

The Kestria Revenue Service processed 92 per cent of complete sales tax refund claims within 15 working days during September. This compares with 86 per cent in August. September payments totalled KRN 18.4 million across 1,760 claims, including claims from manufacturers, wholesalers and building contractors.

The improvement followed the reassignment of six processing staff to the refund team in Ostara. Claims requiring further checks are excluded from the 15-day measure while the service waits for requested information. The published figures include both the number of claims awaiting checks and the reasons for those checks.

At the end of September, 214 claims were awaiting invoices, bank account confirmation or an explanation of unusually large purchases. Businesses can check progress through their tax account. Sending the same claim again can delay processing because staff must establish whether it is a duplicate. A business should instead reply to the information request using its existing claim reference.

Payroll filing service restored after morning access problems

Date: 10/09/2026

Access to the Kestria Revenue Service payroll filing service was restored at 11.40 am today following a technical fault. The interruption began at 8.15 am and affected employers trying to open or submit payroll tax returns. Corporate tax and sales tax filing remained available.

The fault interrupted the connection between the sign-in page and payroll records. Technical checks found no evidence that employer or employee information had been lost or disclosed. Returns submitted before the interruption remain recorded, and employers do not need to send those returns again.

Employers who saw an error message during submission should check their filing history for a receipt number. If no receipt appears, they should reopen the saved return and submit it. The service logged 186 reports from employers, including businesses in Amberford and Kestrel Bay. Anyone still unable to file should contact the payroll support team and quote the message shown on screen.
